title: Prehistoric Landscape Management in the Andean Highlands: Raised Field Agriculture and its Environmental Impact
locator: Population and Environment 13(4):285–300; inspected pp. 289–297, especially chronology p.290, hydrology pp.293–294 and microclimate p.296.
scope_limit: Small reconstructions and archaeological investigation; two reported frost nights do not establish basin-scale averages. Broad sustainability and population-support claims are contested, not adopted here.
evidence_lineage: Author-directed 1981–1986 northern Titicaca fieldwork and experimental reconstruction, plus cited regional work; not an independent replication of Bandy's underlying early yield observations.

title: Energetic efficiency and political expediency in Titicaca Basin raised field agriculture
locator: Journal of Anthropological Archaeology 24:271–296; full article HTML transcription; inspected pp.273–275,280–288.
scope_limit: Column-order transcription imperfect; diagrams not independently inspected. Revival abandonment uses cited Swartley observations, not a new basin census; labour model is schematic. Swartley and Fernández Valdivia/García Chire originals not acquired.
evidence_lineage: Reanalysis of published experimental yields/labour, including Erickson, Kolata, Swartley and Fernández Valdivia/García Chire; dependent on earlier observations, independent in modelling/critique, not independent measurement of all outcomes.

title: Emergent Properties of Balinese Water Temple Networks: Coadaptation on a Rugged Fitness Landscape
source_type: original field research and ecological simulation
locator: American Anthropologist 95(1):97–114; acquired scanned PDF and OCR; inspected pp.100–103,106–111.
scope_limit: Two-river/172-subak model and limited observational calibration; optimality is model-conditional. No claim of a demonstrated historical origin for all Balinese institutions.
evidence_lineage: Original Oos–Petanu simulation and 1988–1989 crop/water observations, drawing on Lansing's earlier fieldwork; Janssen reuses this model, so the two articles are not independent field corroboration.

title: Coordination in irrigation systems: An analysis of the Lansing–Kremer model of Bali
locator: Accessible version is 22 June 2006 uncorrected proof, 21 pp.; inspected introduction pp.2–3, model/optimisation sections2–3 and conclusion pp.19–20. Published Agricultural Systems 93:170–190.
scope_limit: All cited page locators are proof pages, not final pagination. Historical intervention narrative inherits Lansing; independent contribution is model reimplementation and sensitivity analysis.
evidence_lineage: Original Lansing–Kremer source code supplied by its authors; independent reimplementation and optimisation tests; shared underlying ecology/data and inherited historical narrative.

title: Contract Farming and Female Rice Growers in The Gambia
locator: ODI Irrigation Management Network (Africa Edition), Network Paper15, July1992, pp.3–19 within larger compilation; inspected sections3–8, pp.4–18.
scope_limit: Qualitative and historical interpretation, not randomly assigned tenure or compensation; later project yield decline also coincides with prices, soil, repair, diesel and marketing changes.
evidence_lineage: Dissertation fieldwork 1983–1984 and follow-ups 1986–1987 and1990; also cites IFAD and von Braun et al.1989. Some numerical project evidence is shared with AGR-S06, not independent corroboration.

title: Irrigation Technology and Commercialization of Rice in The Gambia: Effects on Income and Nutrition
locator: IFPRI Research Report75,118 pp.; complete scanned report acquired. Read printed pp.9–13,106–108 and survey-design material via OCR (PDF pages10–14,107–109).
scope_limit: Targeted reading, not entire report or regression replication. Largely cross-sectional design; authors explicitly flag latent variables/dependence. Estimates do not randomise project access or gender control.
evidence_lineage: Detailed survey of 200 households/about900 farmers in10 villages including participants/nonparticipants, reported1984–1986 project comparisons. Same project as Carney; her account cites these results.

title: Green Revolution: Impacts, limits, and the path ahead
locator: PNAS109(31):12302–12308; inspected First GR, Limitations of GR-Led Growth Strategies, Environment and Marginal Production Environments.
scope_limit: Review rather than original identification for every statistic. Used for package/adaptation mechanisms, not as independent verification of each cited poverty or diffusion estimate. Forward-looking prescriptions excluded.
evidence_lineage: Synthesises crop-improvement and agricultural-development literature, notably Evenson/Gollin and CGIAR evidence. Likely overlaps national/FAO crop series with AGR-S08; complete genealogy not reconstructed.

title: Two Blades of Grass: The Impact of the Green Revolution
locator: Journal of Political Economy129(8):2344–2384; inspected pp.2346–2347,2358–2365,2378–2379, research design, sample and counterfactual limitations. DOI10.1086/714444.
scope_limit: Country-crop release-timing/shift-share identification depends on parallel relative-yield trends and absence of coincident crop shocks; 90-country baseline excludes specified rich/oil/small cases. No-GR counterfactual excludes alternative innovation and is explicitly qualified by authors.
evidence_lineage: Original compilation/analysis of international variety release dates, initial crop shares and historical crop/FAO data; not independent underlying national measurement from every review using those series.

title: Satellite-based estimates of groundwater depletion in India
source_type: original satellite measurement and hydrological analysis
locator: Nature460:999–1002 plus Methods; inspected study boundary,2002–2008 estimate, alternative storage contributions and uncertainty.
scope_limit: Regional gravity-derived water-storage estimate with modelled component subtraction; does not identify a seed-specific treatment effect, all-India depletion or a current rate.
evidence_lineage: GRACE observations combined with hydrological modelling and ancillary storage/precipitation data; materially different measurement from crop-yield and economic series in AGR-S07–S08.

title: The Profits of Power: Land Rights and Agricultural Investment in Ghana
source_type: original agricultural household/plot survey and econometric analysis
locator: Journal of Political Economy116(6):981–1022; inspected pp.983–988,1002–1018, tables7–9 and conclusion.
scope_limit: Two-year Akwapim survey; inspected survey description does not state exact calendar dates, so case uses late20th-century interval. IV/political-status exclusion restrictions are not equivalent to randomised tenure.
evidence_lineage: Original repeated household/plot survey, plot histories and soil tests in four Akwapim clusters. Same underlying data support multiple estimates in this one paper; no independent replication claimed.

title: Agricultural Decisions after Relaxing Credit and Risk Constraints
locator: Quarterly Journal of Economics129:597–652; inspected pp.599–601, sectionIII,VI.B,VI.D andVIII; tablesIII–IV andIX context; conclusion pp.648–650.
scope_limit: Northern Ghana2009–2011 contracts/sample; insurance and cash treatment magnitudes not directly welfare-equivalent. Investment responses do not settle profit/welfare or commercial-delivery sustainability.
evidence_lineage: Original multiyear randomised cash/insurance grants and random insurance prices, farmer surveys and rainfall triggers. Payout/network analyses share trial participants, not independent experiments supporting each psychological interpretation.

title: Up in Smoke: The Influence of Household Behavior on the Long-Run Impact of Improved Cooking Stoves (2012 working paper)
source_type: original randomized field experiment; working-paper edition
locator: MIT Economics Working Paper12-10, April16/revised April30,2012; acquired complete PDF, inspected introduction, sectionII, results sectionsV–VII, printed pp.27–32 for discussion/conclusion.
scope_limit: This is the2012 working-paper text, not the2016 final journal full text. Trial is one low-cost biomass stove/programme in Odisha and follows outcomes to four years; not all cookstove types.
evidence_lineage: Original phased-randomisation experiment in44 villages/2651 households, starting2006–2007; same experiment and authors as AGR-S16, which is not independent corroboration.

title: Liquefied Petroleum Gas or Biomass for Cooking and Effects on Birth Weight
locator: NEJM387:1735–1746; CDC author manuscript acquired; inspected manuscript pp.6–11 (Methods, coverage/adherence, exposure, birth weight, Discussion). Randomisation May7,2018–February29,2020.
scope_limit: Selected pregnant women/sites in Guatemala,India,Peru,Rwanda; free fuel/stoves and support do not measure unsubsidised uptake. This paper reports birth weight, one of four primary outcomes, not every health endpoint.
evidence_lineage: Original HAPIN randomised intervention and exposure/birth measurements; independent population and technology package from Odisha trial. Background discussion of earlier trials is secondary, not independently reverified here.

title: The Industrial Revolution in the Home: Household Technology and Social Change in the 20th Century
locator: Technology and Culture17(1):1–23; complete web transcription inspected, especially pp.4–10,13–15,21–23.
scope_limit: Middle-class magazine readership is principal documentary population; adverts are neither universal household practice nor causal identification. Figures not directly inspected; original cited archives not separately acquired. Author labels advertising causation and some standards changes as hypotheses.
evidence_lineage: Historical magazines/advertisements, contemporary household investigations and statistics assembled/interpreted by Cowan. Some historical time studies also inform later time-use literature; overlap with Ramey is not fully reconstructed.

title: Time Spent in Home Production in the 20th Century: New Estimates from Old Data
source_type: original historical time-use reconstruction; working-paper edition
locator: NBER Working Paper13985,April2008; inspected introduction, sectionsV–VIII, table6 and early-data discussion. Exact numbers refer to this version, not unacquired2009 journal full text.
scope_limit: Pre1965 observations require harmonisation, grouped-data regression and extrapolation; national reconstruction is not an appliance-specific causal estimate. Home-production definitions and demographic denominators matter.
evidence_lineage: Reanalysis of early time diaries/tabulations plus later representative time-use surveys. Shares historical source traditions with Cowan but provides different quantitative reconstruction; not an independent randomized appliance effect.

title: Up in Smoke: The Influence of Household Behavior on the Long-Run Impact of Improved Cooking Stoves (published abstract)
source_type: published original experiment; abstract access only
locator: American Economic Journal: Economic Policy8(1):80–114; publisher abstract and bibliographic record inspected; DOI10.1257/pol.20140008.
scope_limit: Final journal full text not acquired: AEA showed subscription access, Harvard/J-PAL mirrors returned errors, MIT download rate-limited. Used only to verify central result stated in abstract; no final-table locators claimed.
evidence_lineage: Published version of same Odisha trial as AGR-S12; duplicate edition record retained to expose access boundary, not a second independent study.

title: The Pneumatics of Hero of Alexandria from the original Greek
locator: 1851 edition: editor's preface pp. vii–viii; §50, p. 72 (Pneumatica II.11 in another numbering).
scope_limit: Digitised English edition, not an ancient manuscript or apparatus. Ancient author's exact date and the corpus's transmission are uncertain. Editorial heading is not Hero's terminology. No productive-load test or adoption count in the cited passage.
evidence_lineage: A nineteenth-century translation and editorial reconstruction of a transmitted Greek textual tradition. It is the textual object examined by later scholarship, not independent confirmation of physical deployment.

title: The Mechanical Tradition of Hero of Alexandria: Strategies of Reading from Antiquity to the Early Modern Period
locator: Publisher's 10-page Introduction excerpt, especially pp. 1–4; publisher metadata distinguishes first publication 2023 from paperback 2025.
scope_limit: Only introductory excerpt inspected, not full book. Keyser's original 1992 analysis was encountered through Roby and was not acquired. Purpose of the sphere remains an interpretation.
evidence_lineage: Close interpretation of the Heronian corpus and its reception; shares the ancient textual tradition with ANC-S01. The discussion of Keyser is inherited scholarship, not a separately inspected source.

title: The second century CE Roman watermills of Barbegal: Unraveling the enigma of one of the oldest industrial complexes
locator: Science Advances 4(9), eaar3620. Introduction; Results: microstratigraphy, crystal structure, stable isotope composition; Fig. 4; Discussion. Full article XML acquired at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC6124920/fullTextXML after publisher/PMC browser access failed.
scope_limit: Carbonate samples record selected structures and years. Seasonal interruptions are better supported than identification of customers or hardtack production. Wider claims about Roman growth and empire-wide crises are not independently established here.
evidence_lineage: Original analysis of carbonate fragments from the 1930s Barbegal excavations, surviving museum material and site evidence. ANC-S04 reanalyses overlapping material; the two papers are not independent replications.

title: Operation and decline of the Barbegal mill complex, the largest industrial complex of antiquity
locator: Geoarchaeology 39, pp. 594–608; §§2–5 and especially §6, pp. 606–607. PDF acquired from https://openscience.ub.uni-mainz.de/server/api/core/bitstreams/ed058e41-ee6f-4841-b767-2e2c2dfddaaf/content .
scope_limit: Three reconstructed flumes from the western train do not represent every mill or establish owner identity, profits, or a unique abandonment cause. Do not adopt the title's world-scale superlative as a measured comparative finding.
evidence_lineage: Further analysis and reconstruction of the Barbegal carbonate archive also used by ANC-S03. Adds microstratigraphic/hydraulic interpretation; shares authors, specimens, and much archaeological chronology.

title: The Aqueducts of Rome (De aquaeductu urbis Romae), Book II
locator: Ancient account c. 97–early second century CE; Loeb English edition. Inspected §§94–96, 116–129, especially §§116–118 (workforce and funding), 121–124 (repair scheduling and access).
scope_limit: Official self-presentation and prescriptions are not audited performance records. Reported staffing and finances are for Rome at a particular time, not the entire empire. Translation uses 'wages' for expenses of enslaved gangs; this does not establish free contractual employment.
evidence_lineage: Transmitted text by an imperial water commissioner, including quoted earlier legal measures. Bannon (ANC-S06) uses this same source alongside inscriptions and juristic texts; overlapping propositions are not independent corroboration.

title: Fresh Water in Roman Law: Rights and Policy
locator: Journal of Roman Studies 107, pp. 60–89; inspected Introduction, §III Civic Aqueducts, especially private grants and provincial examples, and §V Conclusion; full Cambridge HTML.
scope_limit: Reconstruction from selected legal, epigraphic and literary evidence, principally late Republic through early Empire. Rights on paper do not measure household access or equal enforcement. Ancient-law analysis, not current legal guidance.
evidence_lineage: Original legal-historical synthesis of Frontinus, municipal inscriptions, and juristic texts transmitted in Justinian's Digest. Specific inscriptions were read through Bannon, not separately inspected; part of the evidence overlaps ANC-S05.

title: Wars, Book V (Gothic War I), chapter 19
locator: Gothic War I.19.8–28 (= Wars V.19.8–28), especially §§13 and 19–28; Loeb volume III.
scope_limit: Literary account of the siege of Rome in 537, written later in the sixth century. Credits Belisarius; statements that mills sufficed for the city are not output measurements. Does not establish the permanent fate of every aqueduct.
evidence_lineage: Ancient narrative with close authorial proximity to the campaign, surviving through textual transmission. The emergency sequence is a single narrative witness, not an independently replicated operational log.

title: Qanāt and Falaj: Polycentric and Multi-Period Innovations: Iran and the United Arab Emirates as Case Studies
locator: Underground Aqueducts Handbook, chapter 17, pp. 279–301; inspected chapter OCR, especially §§17.1–17.2.3 (pp. 280–288) and §§17.3.4–17.4.2 (pp. 293–295).
scope_limit: Archaeological synthesis with explicit disagreements, including shallow versus deeper sources and early Iranian dating. Most underlying excavation reports and luminescence datasets were not acquired. Polycentric origins are argued, not established at every site.
evidence_lineage: Author's comparative archaeological interpretation, drawing on excavations at al-Madam and other UAE sites plus previous Iranian studies. Its treatment of Polybius overlaps ANC-S09; chronology is not an independent dataset for every repeated later citation.

title: Histories, Book X, chapter 28
locator: X.28.1–7, especially §§2–4; Loeb volume IV, pp. 169–171. Describes Antiochus III's Parthian campaign, conventionally 209 BCE, from a later second-century BCE account.
scope_limit: Reports local testimony about earlier Persian rule; not an original grant or construction account. Paton's wording is five generations of cultivation rights, not an explicit tax exemption. The water source is not technically specified. Host notes this page is not fully proofread.
evidence_lineage: Single ancient transmitted narrative. Boucharlat (ANC-S08) critically interprets the same passage. Reading both does not give two independent witnesses to the grant policy.

title: Dujiangyan's Annual Repair System in Ancient Times: From Jianpengyan Inscription by Shu Defender Li Bing in Qin Dynasty (古代都江堰岁修制度——从《秦蜀守李冰湔堋堰官碑》说起)
locator: Journal of Xihua University (Philosophy & Social Sciences) 37(4), pp. 8–18, DOI 10.19642/j.issn.1672-8505.2018.04.002. Inspected attributed Chinese reproduction §§1–5, especially §§1, 2, 4. Publisher metadata/abstract verified; journal PDF failed (404/412).
scope_limit: Substantial reproduction, not independently collated against journal PDF; some apparatus may be missing. English summaries here are our translations. Inscription dates/readings are mediated by Peng; no original rubbing inspected. Qin continuity arguments and triumphal framing require scrutiny.
evidence_lineage: Original historian's argument using excavated Han inscriptions, transmitted histories, and much later records. These are several underlying sources but only Peng's presentation was inspected; modern claims of continuous operation are not independent evidence for each intervening century.

title: Sustainability of the Dujiangyan Irrigation System for over 2000 Years—A Numerical Investigation of the Water and Sediment Dynamic Diversions
locator: Sustainability 12, 2431; §§1, 3–6, especially pp. 2–3 and 12–13. PDF acquired from https://mdpi-res.com/d_attachment/sustainability/sustainability-12-02431/article_deploy/sustainability-12-02431.pdf .
scope_limit: Numerical experiment using particular channel geometry and flow regimes, not an ancient measurement. Omits modern upstream dam effect; notes 1974 modification and further validation needs. Introductory claims of perfectly continuous performance and abandoned ancient systems elsewhere are not accepted as historical findings.
evidence_lineage: Original coupled flow/sediment model drawing on earlier hydraulic studies; historical origin and continuity statements are inherited background. Independent of Peng's inscription analysis for physical modelling, but not an independent historical time series.

title: Archaeological studies at Dholavira using GPR
locator: Current Science 114(4), pp. 879–887; methods pp. 880–881; interpretations pp. 884–886; Conclusion p. 886. Institutional PDF inspected at https://asc.iitgn.ac.in/assets/publications/research_papers/Archaeological_studies_at_Dholavira_using_GPR_Agrawal_Majumder_Bisht_Prashant.pdf .
scope_limit: Unexcavated features and proposed flood mechanism are hypotheses requiring excavation. Abstract/early text gives 12,276 m² but conclusion gives 12,776 m²; exact survey area not adopted. GPR dates the survey, not the ancient destruction.
evidence_lineage: Original GPR measurements collected in 2015, interpreted using existing excavation knowledge, including coauthor Bisht's work. Measurement is new; contextual interpretations partly share the ASI excavation lineage summarised by ANC-S13.

title: Dholavira: A Harappan City (India), No 1645—Advisory Body Evaluation
locator: 13-page standalone evaluation; printed pp. 13–15, especially Description and history, phased settlement and water structures; full PDF accessible through web extraction.
scope_limit: Evaluation based on State Party nomination, excavation material and mission evidence, not the full excavation report. Historical dates and destruction narrative were not independently re-dated. Overall c. 3000–1500 BCE label includes gaps and a final phase reported as c. 1500–1450 BCE.
evidence_lineage: Institutional synthesis relying heavily on ASI excavation and nomination evidence. Shares parts of the archaeological lineage with ANC-S12; does not independently corroborate each reconstruction or proposed cause of decline.

title: Information Management: A Proposal
locator: HTML transcription; Losing Information at CERN; A solution: Hypertext; CERN Requirements; Non requirements. Inspected these sections and the transcription notice.
scope_limit: A proposal and author recollection of Enquire, not measured global adoption. Written March 1989, recirculated May 1990, later HTML transcription; historical errors in incidental references are not endorsed.
evidence_lineage: Original CERN proposal by its author, preserved as a later W 3C-hosted transcription. Direct evidence of proposed requirements; later framing supplied by author.

title: Licensing the Web
locator: Public releases of Web software; Open Source release; The first CERN Open Source software licence; MIT Open Source release.
scope_limit: CERN participant retrospective quotes releases; original signed release not separately acquired. No causal estimate of licensing impact. Broad claims about free-software history and W 3C dates are not used.
evidence_lineage: Retrospective CERN account by institutional participants, reproducing 1993–1995 legal/announcement text; not independent of the CERN institutional tradition or original Web developers.

title: Computer and Internet Use in the United States: 2015 (ACS-37)
locator: pp. 1–3, Figure 1, CPS/ACS comparison box; Tables 1–2 and high-connectivity definition. Full PDF acquired; selected sections inspected.
scope_limit: Households, not persons or active-use minutes. CPS and ACS use different questions/methods. ACS broadband includes mobile and handheld includes more than smartphones.
evidence_lineage: Original Census analysis of CPS historical survey series and 2015 ACS. Figures from these two surveys are distinct series, not independent confirmations of identical levels.

title: Communications Market Report 2015: Internet and online content
locator: Section 5.2; printed pp. 341–347, Figures 5.14–5.20; reported importance question QE 11/QE 40 and base n=3095. Read through web PDF extraction.
scope_limit: Device take-up, household ownership and most-important-device questions have different bases. Report narrative uses inconsistent 2014 smartphone importance percentage; no 2014 percentage used here.
evidence_lineage: Ofcom Technology Tracker W 1 2015, partly combined with commercial audience-measurement sources elsewhere in report. Claims here use the original Ofcom survey, not comScore.

title: The Smartphone Difference / U.S. Smartphone Use in 2015
locator: pp. 1–4, 14–19 and 20–22; smartphone-dependence definitions and survey methods. Full PDF acquired; relevant sections inspected.
scope_limit: Ownership national estimate from November 2014 omnibus polls; usage/financial circumstances from October 2014 American Trends Panel. Dependence has a narrower definition than later smartphone-only indicators. Self-report, not causal assignment.
evidence_lineage: Original Pew omnibus and American Trends Panel surveys with Knight Foundation support. National ownership and panel behavioural estimates are separate samples; repeated summaries within report are not independent evidence.

title: Telecom Statistics India-2024
authors: Economic Research Unit, Department of Telecommunications, Government of India
locator: Table 1.10 p. 14 (PDF p.21); Table 6.2 p.61 (PDF p.68), including period footnote. Full PDF acquired; tables inspected.
scope_limit: Official compilation of TRAI provider returns. Subscription counts are not unique people; revenue per GB is not advertised tariff. Calendar-year data switch to financial years from 2020–21. Nominal rupees.
evidence_lineage: DoT compilation explicitly sources TRAI quarterly/yearly Performance Indicator Reports. Underlying provider administrative returns were not independently audited; DoT and TRAI are not two independent datasets.

title: Annual Status of Education Report (Rural) 2021
locator: Sample Design pp.15–16; Household Survey Major Findings pp.28–31, Tables 8–12 and 2018 comparison footnote. Full PDF acquired; sections inspected.
scope_limit: 2021 telephone sample drawn from prior survey phone numbers; no-phone households excluded from 2018 comparison. Rural children ages 5–16, enrolled-child device tables. Availability is not personal ownership or educational effect.
evidence_lineage: Original ASER survey of 76, 706 households, reaching 75, 234 children, using a frame based on ASER 2018; 2018 comparisons reconstructed to exclude households without mobile phones. Not independent cross-sectional samples with identical coverage.

title: Mobile Money: The Economics of M-PESA (NBER Working Paper 16721)
locator: Sections II–IV; PDF pp.6–11, 13–15, 26–27; printed pp.25–26 Tables 14a–14b. Full PDF acquired through direct retrieval after web tool returned 403 for a different NBER PDF path.
scope_limit: Working paper, not NBER peer review. Some aggregate comparisons and claims of fastest adoption are not used. Author collaboration with Safaricom/Vodafone and survey commissioning by FSD/CBK acknowledged. Survey experience and user composition are observational.
evidence_lineage: Original authors’ 2008/2009 household panel and agent research; some network data supplied by Safaricom. Shares baseline research and authors with DIG-S09, so not independent corroboration of welfare impacts.

title: The long-run poverty and gender impacts of mobile money
locator: Science 354(6317), pp.1288–1292, DOI 10.1126/science.aah 5309; equations 1–2; Tables 1–3; attrition and mechanisms discussion. All five article pages inspected; supplement not acquired.
scope_limit: Publisher-form article hosted by FinDev Gateway; direct PDF succeeded despite web-tool 403. Identification relies on early agent rollout assumptions, fixed effects and controls; substantial attrition, Nairobi later excluded. Extrapolated national poverty total is not a count. Supplemental robustness tables not independently inspected.
evidence_lineage: Original five-wave 2008–2014 household panel, extending the data programme in DIG-S08; uses earlier research’s falsification and rollout tests. This analysis is not an independent replication of those earlier findings.

title: 2024 FinAccess Household Survey Main Report
locator: Survey Design and Methodology pp.3–5 (PDF pp.15–17); Figure 2.3 p.12; usage section p.26. Full PDF acquired by direct retrieval after web timeout.
scope_limit: Interview target 16+, but substantive access/use analysis is adults 18+. Current-use responses cover all mobile-money providers, not M-PESA alone or active accounts within a stated monthly window. Institution has financial-inclusion policy interests.
evidence_lineage: New national household survey based on Kenya Household Master Sample Frame from 2019 census, separate from Suri/Jack panel. Institutional partnership with FSD and CBK overlaps earlier research commissioning but observations are a different survey.

title: Online Nation 2024 Report
locator: pp.66–69, especially p.68 and footnote 178; web PDF extraction inspected.
scope_limit: p.68 reports 4% VR gaming in 2023 followed by an inconsistent 3%:2023 parenthesis. Underlying DIG-S15 establishes the 4% level; no growth rate inferred. Nearby console/phone statistics use different trackers/years.
evidence_lineage: Secondary presentation of Ofcom Adults’ Media Literacy Tracker 2023, Technology Tracker 2024 and commercial Ampere sources. Its VR figure repeats DIG-S15; it is not independent corroboration.

title: Quantifying the Effects of Working in VR for One Week
locator: Author version arXiv:2206.03189v 2, 8 June 2022; sections 3.1–3.4, 3.6–3.7 and 4; PDF pp.1–5, 8–9.
scope_limit: 16 university employee/researcher completers plus two withdrawals; counterbalanced own-work study. Quest 2/remote-desktop/K830 setup deliberately matches conventional display; not an optimised spatial workspace. Subjective productivity is not objective output. Some authors affiliated with Microsoft Research.
evidence_lineage: Original controlled within-subjects study at three physical locations in Germany, with study dataset offered by authors. Later behavioural analyses of this study would not be independent samples.

title: Meta Platforms, Inc. Form 10-K for year ended December 31, 2023
locator: Part I Reality Labs Products and relevant risk discussion; Note 16 Segment and Geographical Information, printed pp.124–125; segment revenue/operating-loss table.
scope_limit: Commercial company disclosure. Audited segment finances do not identify headset users, retention or per-device subsidy. Segment includes AR, mixed reality and VR; allocations and research costs prevent treating loss as cost of observed VR consumption.
evidence_lineage: Company accounting and management disclosures filed with SEC; no separate original adoption dataset used here. SEC hosting is not an independent estimate of market adoption.

title: Microsoft 2015 Annual Report
locator: Shareholder letter; Create more personal computing; MD&A Phone Hardware; Impairment, Integration, and Restructuring Expenses.
scope_limit: Commercial management narrative and accounting disclosure. FY 2014 phone sales only post-Nokia acquisition; 2015 versus 2014 sales growth not comparable full years. Non-Lumia is not equivalent to Windows Phone. Impairment is neither user count nor causal attribution.
evidence_lineage: Company annual accounts, acquisition-related valuations and management strategy; no independent carrier, developer or consumer causal dataset. Narrative and figures originate in the same company.

title: Adults’ Media Literacy Core Survey 2023 Data Tables
locator: Table 70 M 6A printed pp.292–294 (PDF pp.298–300); Table 74 G 1 printed pp.307–308 (PDF pp.313–314); fieldwork 27 September–12 November 2023.
scope_limit: 3, 643 UK adults 16+, mixed quota interviews; G 1 multi-code, no monthly/weekly recall threshold. M 6A base is 3, 351 unweighted smartphone users, weighted base 3, 231; task difficulty is a perception. Percentages are rounded.
evidence_lineage: Original tabulations from Ofcom 2023 Core Survey. DIG-S11 repeats these gaming data; DIG-S16 documents this same sample, not another independent survey.

title: Adults’ Media Literacy Research 2023 Technical Report
locator: pp.4–5 methodological/trend notes; pp.7–8 Core study sampling, interviewing and reporting.
scope_limit: Methodological documentation of a quota sample, not a separate adoption observation. Adults, not households, are the target for weighted reported proportions. 2021 trend comparisons are only indicative because methods changed.
evidence_lineage: Methods for the same original 2023 Core Survey tabulated in DIG-S15 and summarised in DIG-S11. Provides denominator/sampling provenance, not independent effect corroboration.

title: Beyond the learning curve: factors influencing cost reductions in photovoltaics
locator: Energy Policy 34, 3218–3232; inspected pp. 3221, 3224–3228, especially Tables 2–3 and §§3.1–4.4; cached PDF pages 4, 7–11.
scope_limit: Engineering decomposition of crystalline-silicon module costs/prices, 1975–2001, not system electricity costs or identified policy effects; early market-quality changes leave a large residual.
evidence_lineage: Author reconstructs technical/cost inputs from Maycock industry series, laboratory efficiency histories, company and institutional reports. Kavlak et al. subsequently reuse some of this evidence and revise the decomposition; they are not wholly independent corroboration.

title: Evaluating the causes of cost reduction in photovoltaic modules
locator: Energy Policy 123, 700–710; inspected §§2–4.2, pp. 701–707, Table 3, Figures 3–5 and conclusion; local PDF.
scope_limit: Cost-equation decomposition and judgment-based allocation to R&D, learning and scale; the 60% market-policy attribution additionally assumes a public/private R&D split and equal effectiveness. Supplemental data were not independently re-estimated.
evidence_lineage: Reconstructed industry technical/cost observations, including Nemet (2006), NREL efficiency records and materials/industry studies. Same research group and conceptual method as ENE-S11; recurrence across those models is not independent causal identification.

title: Innovation and international technology transfer: The case of the Chinese photovoltaic industry (CERNA Working Paper 2010-12; HAL version 1)
locator: Inspected working-paper pp. 1–11, 17–18 and Appendices 1–2; PDF pp. 3–13, 19–20, 24–28. Published version appeared in Energy Policy 39 (2011), 761–770; that version was not silently substituted.
scope_limit: Interviews and patent/equipment proxies cover early Chinese PV entry, principally 2003–2009; patent counts miss tacit and secret process innovation. Small, producer-centered interview sample cannot represent workers or all firms.
evidence_lineage: Authors combine 79,642 patent records, equipment-provider listings, ten interviews including a university institute (Appendix 1 lists nine companies), company biographies and inherited EPIA/REDP/industry output statistics. Abstract calls these ten companies; this discrepancy is retained rather than harmonized.

title: Historical construction costs of global nuclear power reactors
locator: Web-parsed full article available; inspected §§2–4.4, §5, Table 1, especially pp. 373–375, 378–381. Local direct PDF request returned 403; inspected extracts retained in cache/web-inspections.json.
scope_limit: 349-reactor, seven-country overnight-cost compilation centered on completed reactors as of 2015; missing major countries, cancelled projects and some experimental routes. Interest during construction excluded. Source text says 26 Korean reactor records while Table 1 cohort counts imply a different total; no subgroup count is reproduced here.
evidence_lineage: Reuses US Koomey–Hultman/EIA/early AEC evidence; French Cour des Comptes 2012 data; Korean utility inquiry with KHNP/NABO/KPX checks; other national compilations. Not independent of the earlier nuclear cost literature for reused reactors. Underlying reactor files were not re-audited here.

title: The French Pressurized Water Reactor Program
locator: Historical case study for Global Energy Assessment Chapter 24; inspected pp. 2–3, 5–10, Table 1 and §§2–4.
scope_limit: Author synthesis of his 2009/2010 reconstruction, not a second independent French dataset. Its broad assertion of universal negative learning is not adopted; later national comparisons contest it.
evidence_lineage: Uses Grubler 2009/2010 reconstructions from French public/parliamentary accounts, IAEA dates and institutional histories including Jasper and Finon–Staropoli. French cost data precede the reactor-level Cour des Comptes series used by ENE-S04.

title: Sources of Cost Overrun in Nuclear Power Plant Construction Call for a New Approach to Engineering Design
locator: Author manuscript web text; inspected abstract, §§2.1–2.2 and §4.4, manuscript pp. 1–5, 10–11; publication Joule 4, 2348–2373. Direct download returned 429; extracts cached.
scope_limit: Detailed 1976–1987 cost-account model concerns a Westinghouse four-loop plant; 2017 containment data concern a narrow recent US project context. Indirect-cost reallocations and counterfactual component costs require assumptions; no labour-income panel.
evidence_lineage: Combines IAEA, EIA and published reactor histories with Department of Energy EEDB accounts and construction/engineering reports. Some underlying US reactor history overlaps ENE-S04; the component-account decomposition contributes additional evidence, not a wholly independent national history.

title: US3025589A: Method of manufacturing semiconductor devices
locator: Filed 1 May 1959; issued 20 March 1962. Inspected specification opening and claim 1 in hosted patent transcription; local HTML/text retained.
scope_limit: A patent discloses and claims a technical process; it does not demonstrate factory yields, licensing uptake, commercial success or a unique first inventor. Host metadata priority chains are not used to date the planar demonstration.
evidence_lineage: US patent record as transcribed by Google Patents, assigned to Fairchild. Patent also cited by ENE-S14, so the latter is not independent corroboration of the same disclosed process.

title: Computers in Spaceflight: The NASA Experience — Chapter 2, Evolution of the hardware
locator: NASA history, printed pp. 31–34; inspected entire supplied subsection, especially NOR-gate standardization, procurement and note references 30–35.
scope_limit: Retrospective official history with participant disagreement. Its estimate that Apollo used 60% of US microcircuit output in summer 1963 is a narrow-period claim, not the whole decade or all semiconductor output. Underlying note 34 was not separately retrieved.
evidence_lineage: NASA-commissioned historical reconstruction using program documents and interviews identified in endnotes. We inspected the historical account, not the original procurement invoices. No reliance on its possibly ambiguous Block I/Block II labeling or cycle-time units.

title: Learning-by-Doing Spillovers in the Semiconductor Industry
locator: Journal of Political Economy 102(6), 1200–1227; inspected pp. 1200–1203, 1210–1215, 1219–1224, Tables 1, 4–7; local PDF.
scope_limit: Quarterly Dataquest merchant DRAM shipments/prices, 1974Q1–1992Q4, 32 firms; firm costs and plant yields not directly observed. Cournot behavior, demand elasticity and instruments matter; vertically integrated internal producers excluded.
evidence_lineage: Original econometric analysis of proprietary Dataquest prices and firm shipments; earlier qualitative yield examples are inherited OECD/industry evidence. Seven DRAM generations plus a distinct 16K voltage variant; not eight independent technology histories.

title: Brief History and Future of the Lithium-Ion Battery — Nobel Lecture
locator: Inspected historical §§1.1–1.5 and opening of §2, printed pp. 207–217, via web text. Direct PDF returned 403. Forecast passages excluded from this contribution.
scope_limit: Inventor retrospective emphasizing his team; patent chronology and qualitative impact-test account are not an independently audited safety dataset or complete commercialization history. No claim that lithium-ion cells are hazard-free.
evidence_lineage: First-person account referring to Whittingham 1976, Mizushima/Goodenough 1980, Yoshino patents and 2012 retrospective. Original laboratory notebooks and full commercial qualification records not inspected.

title: Determinants of lithium-ion battery technology cost decline
locator: Energy & Environmental Science 14, 6074–6098; inspected data/method sections pp. 6076–6078 and results pp. 6085–6091, Figures 5–9, Table 4, via web text. Direct download returned 403; extracts retained.
scope_limit: Representative high-energy-density cylindrical 18650 cell configurations for 1995–2000 and 2010–2015, not all battery chemistries or EV packs. Sparse historical inputs, estimated manufacturing parameters and assumed allocations limit causal attribution.
evidence_lineage: Authors assemble literature measurements, technical reports, materials prices and production estimates into a new cell-cost model. Shares conceptual method and some authors with ENE-S02; price validation draws on their separate compiled price series, not independent factory accounts.

title: The future of electric two-wheelers and electric vehicles in China
locator: Energy Policy 36, 2544–2555; inspected §§1.2–2.4, §3 and historical parts of §6, particularly pp. 2545–2550 and 2553. Web-parsed text retained; direct request returned empty 202.
scope_limit: Mixed industry estimates, observations in ten cities, manufacturer/user interviews and six assembly-plant visits; descriptive force-field rankings are subjective. Forecasts excluded; samples not nationally representative.
evidence_lineage: Builds on authors’ 2007 studies and 2006–2007 fieldwork plus CMIC/CNBS/Jamerson industry series. Shares authors, survey evidence and underlying transport/lead research with ENE-S13; not independent replication.

title: Comparative environmental impacts of electric bikes in China
locator: Transportation Research Part D 14, 281–290; inspected §§2–4, Tables 2 and 6, especially pp. 283–284 and 287–289; local PDF.
scope_limit: Partial life-cycle inventory, regional grid assumptions and passenger-load/lifespan scenarios; not measured health damages or a full lifecycle account. Several bus/car factors borrowed from non-Chinese or earlier studies. Battery-price comparison approximate.
evidence_lineage: Combines authors’ field/transport work, industrial statistical intensities, regional grid factors and Mao et al. 2006 lead-flow estimates based on 1999 data. Shares earlier user evidence with ENE-S12. No independent blood-lead cohort is established by this analysis.

title: 1959: Invention of the “Planar” Manufacturing Process
locator: The Silicon Engine timeline entry; inspected main account and references; downloaded HTML/text.
scope_limit: Museum synthesis provides commercial chronology and failure-mode context, not a production-yield series. Its expansive significance claims are not repeated.
evidence_lineage: Explicitly draws on Hoerni patent/1960 paper, Lécuyer 2006, Moore 1998, Riordan 2007 and oral history; same patent as ENE-S07. Those underlying works, apart from the patent, were not independently read here.

title: De re metallica, translated from the 1556 Latin edition
locator: Book II, printed pp. 31–33 (water, roads, provisioning and rulers); Book VI, pp. 171–185 (pumping choices, replacement teeth, staged pumps). Selected text sections inspected; complete HTML available.
scope_limit: Technical treatise, not an installation census. Translation and editorial notes are later; claim uses authorial text rather than assigning the Hoovers’ historical annotations to Agricola. Illustrations do not establish prevalence.
evidence_lineage: Direct historical authorial text in a 1912 translation/reprint; later editor notes distinguished. No new archival sample. Multhauf (IND-S02) also relies on Agricola, so these are not independent evidence for the same described pump.

title: Mine Pumping in Agricola’s Time and Later
locator: Printed pp. 114–120; especially pp. 117–120 and footnotes 13–22. Main text and relevant notes inspected in full HTML.
scope_limit: Smithsonian historical study based on treatises and depictions; some proposed dates conflict. Images are selective and sometimes internally inconsistent. Its hydraulic explanation for German steam delay is a conjecture, not an identified causal result.
evidence_lineage: Technical treatises (Agricola, Lohneyss, Calvör and later histories), mine-manager report transmitted through an 1898 edition, and mining coin imagery. Some lineage overlaps IND-S01; prior authors’ installation statements not directly re-audited.

title: Collective Invention during the British Industrial Revolution: The Case of the Cornish Pumping Engine
locator: ECIS Working Paper 04.02, printed pp. 10–20, 22 (PDF pp. 12–22, 24); figure 1 located p. 32. Sections 3–4 inspected. Downloaded PDF and extracted text retained locally.
scope_limit: The inspected object is the 2004 working paper, not the journal pagination. Reconstructs published engineering evidence; Lean’s original reports and royalty contracts not independently inspected. Information sharing, investment and high-pressure engineering changed together.
evidence_lineage: Boulton/Watt and Cornish engineering histories, Lean/Pole duty reporting and reconstructed patents/ownership. Works by Hills, Barton, Rowe and von Tunzelmann mediate much evidence; the last also informs IND-S04. Not independent archival corroboration of all claims.

title: Productivity Growth in the Industrial Revolution: A New Growth Accounting Perspective
locator: January 2002 version, pp. 13–19 and table 3 on p. 23. Downloaded full PDF; those analytic passages and table inspected.
scope_limit: Working-paper estimates, not silently substituted for either 2004 published article. Reconstructed horsepower, capital shares and social savings depend on assumptions; sectoral importance is not the same as aggregate growth contribution. No claim that the results settle later revisions to steam stocks.
evidence_lineage: Reconstructed engine horsepower and costs from Kanefsky, Musson and von Tunzelmann, national accounts, and railway social savings. Some inherited engineering literature overlaps IND-S03. This analysis contributes accounting, not a new installation census.

title: Limited waterpower contributed to rise of steam power in British “Cottonopolis”
locator: Abstract, introduction, “Impact on the British textile industry”, and methods passages on hydropower estimation and mill census retrieved and inspected. DOI 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgae251. Some later open attempts returned an access challenge.
scope_limit: Not all article sections or supplementary files were acquired. Physical reconstruction uses terrain, historical climate and assumed efficiency; modern marginal-cost thresholds are suggestive, not observed historical adoption prices. Does not independently identify labour-control motives or reservoir feasibility.
evidence_lineage: New combination of terrain/historical climate, archival factory reports and a cartographic mill census. Historical interpretation also inherits earlier water/steam literature. Only specified text sections inspected; supplements and raw reconstruction not audited.

title: Fleeing the Flowing Commons: Robert Thom, Water Reservoir Schemes, and the Shift to Steam Power in Early Nineteenth-Century Britain
locator: Author-institution repository abstract and bibliographic record; journal reference Environmental History 19(1), pp. 55–77. Full text not acquired.
scope_limit: Only supports an attributed summary of Malm’s argument about proposed reservoirs and coordination. Scheme-level costs, archives and the article’s strong cheaper-water conclusion were not audited. Do not cite detailed pages as if read.
evidence_lineage: Abstract identifies Robert Thom and Lancashire reservoir proposals as historical material; exact archival and cost lineage unknown because the full article was not acquired.

title: The British Industrial Revolution in Global Perspective: chapter 1 excerpt
locator: Publisher excerpt, chapter 1, pp. 1–10 available; pp. 1–5 inspected, especially pp. 1–3 on factor prices and engineering-led diffusion.
scope_limit: Introductory formulation only: underlying profitability computations, full wage series and later replies to critics were not inspected. Supports attribution of the thesis rather than a verified finding that technology was uneconomic everywhere outside Britain.
evidence_lineage: Introductory argument summarising Allen’s larger wage, price and profitability work; underlying series not inspected in this excerpt. Shares a factor-price debate with IND-S08 and IND-S11, not independent corroboration of their figures.

title: Spinning the Industrial Revolution
locator: Accepted-manuscript pp. 4, 15–16, 25–32, 37–41 and dataset table 6. These pages inspected in locally downloaded 58-page PDF; journal version is Economic History Review 72(1), pp. 126–155.
scope_limit: Archival research, but individual archive originals not independently inspected. Most reconstructed observations concern wool; pre-factory cotton data are scarce. Full-time work and daily earnings require inference. Challenges wage premise more directly than it identifies alternative invention motives.
evidence_lineage: New assembled archival/printed pay and productivity observations, including workhouses, putting-out accounts, schools and personal records; debates prior Muldrew/Allen estimates. Individual archive originals not directly inspected here.

title: The Philosophy of Manufactures (selected passages)
locator: Fordham extract inspected, identified as original pp. 5–8, 14–15, 20–21, 23, 29–31; especially paragraphs beginning “The principle of the factory system”, “By the infirmity”, and “In the infancy of mechanical engineering”.
scope_limit: Contemporary pro-factory advocacy, not neutral observation of workers’ welfare. The extract does not map each paragraph individually to a printed page. Page ranges are the compiler’s provenance, and paragraph incipits are the exact reading locators.
evidence_lineage: Direct passages from Ure’s 1835 treatise transmitted by a sourcebook compiler; authorial views are evidence for advocacy. Ure also appears in IND-S08, so the shared quotation is not two independent observers.

title: Connecting the Scientific and Industrial Revolutions: The Role of Practical Mathematics
locator: UCD WP20/17, sections 2.1–2.3, printed pp. 13–18 (PDF pp. 15–20), and p. 27. Downloaded full PDF; specified passages inspected.
scope_limit: Working-paper historical mechanism argument drawing on technical biographies and earlier studies. Does not identify an exogenous skill-supply effect or establish that every machine depended on instrument-making. No numerical horsepower claim from its p. 16 is reused.
evidence_lineage: Historical argument drawing on Musson/Robinson, Cookson, Rolt, Roe, biographies and contemporary engineering statements. Directly acquired paper, not original factory archives. Some engineering histories overlap other industrial sources.

title: Cotton Textiles and the Great Divergence: Lancashire, India and Shifting Competitive Advantage, 1600–1850
locator: CEPR Discussion Paper 5183; printed pp. 2–4, 11, 15–25, 27, 32–33 and tables 7–13 located. Downloaded full 50-page PDF; relevant passages inspected. Printed pagination is three less than PDF page number.
scope_limit: This is the earlier discussion paper, not the 2009 journal version. Wage units and household assistants are imperfectly comparable; productivity partly inferred from prices and assumed Indian stagnation. Protection’s causal effect remains disputed.
evidence_lineage: Trade returns and wage observations inherited through historians including Chaudhuri, Wadsworth/Mann, Gilboy and Young; productivity partly inferred from price studies. Shares data and literature with IND-S12 and IND-S13; not three independent measurements of India’s decline.

title: Mughal Decline, Climate Change, and Britain’s Industrial Ascent: An Integrated Perspective on India’s 18th and 19th Century Deindustrialization
locator: NBER Working Paper 11730; sections 2–7, especially printed pp. 15–19, 24–28 and model at p. 19. Selected sections inspected in downloaded PDF; published successor appeared in 2008.
scope_limit: The specified working paper models price evidence, with mobile labour, subsistence-linked wages and initially non-traded grain. Not causal identification of climate or Mughal decline; sparse employment evidence and inherited aggregate manufacturing estimates are not reproduced as fresh measurements.
evidence_lineage: Compiled relative prices, wages and drought/political histories; incorporates Broadberry/Gupta and earlier national/manufacturing reconstructions. Its model is new analysis of partly shared evidence, not independent observation of the same industrial-output ratios.

title: Atlantic Slavery and the Rise of the Capitalist Global Economy
locator: Full HTML article; sections I–II on regional wages and Atlantic markets, section III and table 2 on commodity production, section IV paragraphs on Charles Grant and table 3 on Indian trade inspected.
scope_limit: Argument by a participating historian, including primary testimony quoted through other scholarship. Neither the parliamentary original nor underlying trade returns independently acquired. Broad claims of slavery’s necessity and colonial policy effects are not cleanly separated by an experiment.
evidence_lineage: Author’s prior Atlantic trade research plus cited regional wage and colonial-trade studies; Charles Grant testimony via Chaudhuri. Substantial literature overlap with IND-S11/12. Claims about market formation are interpretation, not an independent experimental sample.

title: National Leadership and Competing Technological Paradigms: The Globalization of Cotton Spinning, 1878–1933
locator: Journal of Economic History 70(3), pp. 535–566. Author-linked public PDF downloaded; pp. 535–542, 548–554, 558–561 and tables 1–3 inspected. Author index: https://gavin-wright.humsci.stanford.edu/recent-papers-and-publications
scope_limit: British supplier order records cover much world machinery trade, not every installed machine or realised mill outcome. Technical specification proxies, selective recorded cotton types and nonexperimental adoption models limit causal inference; explanations of Indian labour relations are qualified in the text.
evidence_lineage: Newly analysed archived British machinery-supplier orders/specifications, plus installed-spindle compilations, technical manuals and worker histories. Relative performance uses proxies; observed orders and historical explanations have distinct evidential bases.

title: Women’s Work and the Politics of Homespun in Socialist China, 1949–1980
locator: International Review of Social History 57, pp. 365–391. Complete PDF retrieved through web; pp. 365–374 inspected. Claims in this contribution use historical background pp. 369–374, not later collectivisation episodes.
scope_limit: Major research focus is post-1949; pre-1949 quantities and history depend on earlier studies, especially Xu and Min, Kraus, Feuerwerker and rural surveys, not independently inspected. Reported handloom-output share is retained as an attributed estimate, not a census audit.
evidence_lineage: Pre-1949 section synthesises Feuerwerker, Xu/Min, Kraus, Fong, rural surveys and gender scholarship (Mann/Bray). Later archival/interview research is not projected backward. The reported 70% estimate is inherited, not newly measured here.

title: From Shafts to Wires: Historical Perspective on Electrification
locator: Journal of Economic History 43(2), pp. 347–372. Full PDF downloaded; pp. 353–363 and 368–372 inspected, especially drive configurations, equipment redesign and utility services.
scope_limit: Technical literature and reconstructed capacity series are stronger for engineering mechanisms than worker experience. No comprehensive unit-drive census exists; horsepower shares cannot be read as establishment adoption rates. Productivity interpretation is not an experimental estimate.
evidence_lineage: Contemporary engineering journals, manufacturers’ descriptions, technical textbooks and reconstructed census/capacity data (including DuBoff). Direct original articles generally not independently acquired. IND-S04 cites related electricity literature, so apparent agreement may share ancestors.

title: Organizational and Economic Obstacles to Automation: A Cautionary Tale from AT&T in the Twentieth Century
authors: James Feigenbaum and Daniel P. Gross
locator: Publisher abstract and author page https://jamesfeigenbaum.github.io/research/att/
scope_limit: Detailed archival mechanism not independently re-read in the full article; use only bounded author-summary claims. Author page retains an earlier title.
evidence_lineage: Authors’ AT&T archival research; related to LBR-S02 and not independent corroboration of the same corporate history.

title: Answering the Call of Automation: How the Labor Market Adjusted to Mechanizing Telephone Operation
authors: James Feigenbaum and Daniel P. Gross
locator: Published QJE 139(3), pp.1879–1939; inspected introduction, §§III–IV, VI–VII and conclusion; especially pp.1895–1897,1906–1908,1923–1928,1934
scope_limit: Observational staggered-adoption study, predominantly small-city US comparison; cohort results focus on white American-born women 16–25. Incumbent linkage is selective and adjusted, not random. Raw data/appendix estimates not replicated.
evidence_lineage: AT&T records, historical newspapers, complete-count US census/IPUMS and FamilySearch genealogical links. Linked outcomes and cohort comparisons partly share the same census and cutover evidence.

title: New Frontiers: The Origins and Content of New Work, 1940–2018
authors: David Autor, Caroline Chin, Anna Salomons and Bryan Seegmiller
locator: QJE 139(3), pp.1399–1465; inspected §II.B pp.1410–1412, §II.C pp.1413–1419, Tables IV/V discussion pp.1435–1442
scope_limit: US title-based measurement and patent matching. Employment in new micro-titles is imputed from title shares, not directly counted; patents do not capture all innovation. No replication performed.
evidence_lineage: Successive Census Alphabetical Index editions, census microdata, Dictionary of Occupational Titles and US patent texts. Title, patent and employment claims derive from the same constructed database.

title: Automation and New Tasks: How Technology Displaces and Reinstates Labor
locator: JEP 33(2), pp.3–30; introduction pp.3–5 and publisher abstract inspected
scope_limit: Task-allocation framework and empirical decomposition, not an unconditional theorem about all historical labour markets or a forecast.
evidence_lineage: Theoretical model and industry-level decomposition; distinguish model predictions from independently observed case outcomes.

title: Early Pottery at 20,000 Years Ago in Xianrendong Cave, China
locator: Science 336:1696–1700; inspected pottery description, dating/context argument, Tables 1–2 and discussion through author-uploaded full-text extraction. DOI 10.1126/science.1218643.
scope_limit: Dates associated deposits, not an invention event; supplementary micromorphology and dating files not independently acquired. No regional diffusion denominator.
evidence_lineage: Original Xianrendong dating/context study combines 1993–2000 excavations and earlier dates with 2009 resampling; 45 dated samples discussed, including 13 from the reopened profiles. This is one site archive, not independent replications.

title: The impact of environmental change on the use of early pottery by East Asian hunter-gatherers
locator: PNAS 115:7931–7936; introduction; Results and Discussion; Table 1; Conclusion; Methods.
scope_limit: 801 samples, not 801 statistically independent households; chemical preservation and detectability constrain inference about all foods. Supporting raw datasets not reanalysed.
evidence_lineage: Original residue study combines newly analysed Japanese ceramics/residues with previously published results for 801 samples at 46 sites. Pooled samples and earlier papers in this research programme are not independent household observations.

title: The Transition from Bronze to Iron in Canaan: Chronology, Technology, and Context
locator: Radiocarbon 57:285–305; pp. 286–300, particularly technological analyses, copper production, and discussion; author-uploaded full-text extraction. DOI 10.2458/azu_rc.57.18563.
scope_limit: Several chemical/metallographic datasets are explicitly unpublished in this synthesis. Association of workshops with administrations is an interpretation. Excavation counts are not population adoption rates.
evidence_lineage: Regional synthesis with authors’ analyses of provenanced objects and production debris, plus inherited excavation chronologies. Some chemical/metallographic datasets unpublished. Object counts, workshop claims and chemical claims overlap the same site histories.

title: The earliest use of iron in China
locator: Metals in Antiquity, BAR International Series 792, pp. 1–9; web-layout copy, sections 1, 3 and 4, especially 3.4 and 4.
scope_limit: Older reconstruction retained to document revision, not treated as the latest chronology. Author distinguishes properly published finds from doubtful tomb contexts; diffusion and economic motives remain interpretive.
evidence_lineage: Scholarly reconstruction from Chinese excavation/metallography publications; explicitly revises the author’s earlier account. Many of these finds recur in MAT-S15, so the two articles are not independent origin evidence.

title: Blast Furnaces in Song–Yuan China
locator: East Asian Science, Technology, and Medicine 18:41–74; pp. 41–43, 51–53, 58–63, especially p. 42 n. 6 and p. 61.
scope_limit: Combines excavations, translated records and engineering inference; exact mineral-fuel chemistry and product allocation remain uncertain. Older study; not a national output dataset.
evidence_lineage: Combines reported furnace excavations, Song fiscal records, Su Shi’s poem, earlier carbon measurements and engineering comparison. Original Chinese records and underlying laboratory reports were not independently read here.

title: Iron Smelting in Sudan: Experimental Archaeology at The Royal City of Meroe
locator: Journal of Field Archaeology 43(5):399–416; introduction, experimental campaigns, Tables 2–4, Lessons Learned and Conclusion, pp. 412–415. PDF acquired locally and text inspected.
scope_limit: Replica reflects later/post-Meroitic workshops; multiple parameters changed together. Later results described as anecdotal without detailed quantification. Demonstrates a viable reconstruction, not unique ancient operation.
evidence_lineage: Original modern Meroe smelting experiments informed by archaeological workshops and local materials. Shares project context and inherited chronology with MAT-S07, but the experimental dataset differs from its charcoal analysis.

title: Fuel selection during long-term ancient iron production in Sudan
locator: Azania 54(1):33–54; pp. 34–39, 45–50, Tables 1–2, Discussion and Conclusions; full-text author/repository reproduction. DOI 10.1080/0067270X.2019.1578567.
scope_limit: 1,754 charcoal fragments across metallurgical and comparison contexts; small and imperfectly matched non-metallurgical sample. Charcoal selection is not a direct census of woodland or proof of management.
evidence_lineage: Original anthracology of 1,754 fragments from Meroe/Hamadab, including metallurgical and comparison contexts. Shares sites and the Humphris research programme with MAT-S06; production chronology partly inherited from another paper not independently inspected.

title: Arsenic Bronze: Dirty Copper or Chosen Alloy? A View from the Americas
locator: Journal of Field Archaeology 23(4):477–514; pp. 477–481, 500–508, Tables 4–6 and Figs. 25–27; full-text extraction inspected.
scope_limit: Controlled modern alloy tests establish properties, not historical motive by themselves. Some elongation measures need more reproducible experiments. Archaeological and political generalisations rely on cited studies not all independently read.
evidence_lineage: Original mechanical-property experiments plus interpretations of previously analysed American artefacts and earlier scholarship. Shares lead researcher, some archaeological references and research questions with MAT-S09; those papers do not independently corroborate Inka policy.

title: The Production of Copper–Arsenic Alloys (Arsenic Bronze) by Cosmelting: Modern Experiment, Ancient Practice
locator: Journal of Archaeological Science 26:497–526; abstract, experimental design, Table 11, discussion pp. 523–526; full article text visible through public reproduction. DOI 10.1006/jasc.1998.0324.
scope_limit: Modern experiments with Peruvian ores and archaeologically informed furnace forms; do not identify the actual process at every ancient site. Claims about ancient emissions are not measured ancient exposure.
evidence_lineage: Original analysis of cosmelting experiments conducted in 1984 with Peruvian ores and archaeologically informed furnace designs. Ancient-process comparison inherits Batán Grande work; not an independent excavation of every site invoked.

title: Sound, color and meaning in the metallurgy of Ancient West Mexico
locator: World Archaeology 27(1):100–115; publisher abstract inspected; full article inaccessible through attempted publisher link.
scope_limit: Only abstract inspected. It identifies tools/status objects and sound/colour interpretation but cannot support numerical prevalence, detailed alloys, or audit of ethnohistoric passages.
evidence_lineage: Abstract of the original researcher’s interpretation combining laboratory work with ethnohistoric/linguistic evidence. Object-level samples and historical passages not inspected. Substantial intellectual overlap with MAT-S11 is expected; exact dataset overlap unknown.

title: Ancient West Mexican Metallurgy: South and Central American Origins and West Mexican Transformations
locator: American Anthropologist 90(4):832–855; publisher abstract and bibliographic information inspected.
scope_limit: Diffusion argument not independently audited beyond abstract. Its circa AD 800 starting date differs from the circa AD 600 framework in the later paper; neither is used as a securely identified first invention.
evidence_lineage: Abstract from Hosler’s West Mexican research programme proposing external technical roots and local changes. The analytical corpus and transfer argument were not fully inspected; this is not independent corroboration of MAT-S10.

title: The Glass Making Crucibles from Ile-Ife, SW Nigeria
locator: Journal of African Archaeology 16:31–59; pp. 31–32 abstract and introduction inspected in PDF extraction; subsequent retrievals timed out. DOI 10.1163/21915784-20180002.
scope_limit: Detailed body tables were not inspected; only explicit abstract-level findings about ten analysed crucibles, refractory clay and estimated 1–7 L capacities are used. Capacity is not annual output.
evidence_lineage: Partial access to crucible analyses associated with the Babalola Igbo Olokun research programme. Shares excavation setting and production interpretation with MAT-S13; material-specific crucible observations are not a second independent workshop discovery.

title: Chemical analysis of glass beads from Igbo Olokun, Ile-Ife (SW Nigeria): New light on raw materials, production, and interregional interactions
locator: Journal of Archaeological Science 90:92–105; sections 2, 3.4, 4.1–4.3 and 5; Table 3 and discussion of sampling and disturbed deposits. DOI 10.1016/j.jas.2017.12.005.
scope_limit: 52 beads selected to cover visible diversity, about 0.5% of excavated assemblage; no statistical population sample. Disturbed deposits and no intact furnace in these units limit chronology and organisation.
evidence_lineage: Original chemical analysis of 52 selected beads from 2011–2012 Igbo Olokun excavations, alongside comparisons with older collections. Shares excavation and researchers with MAT-S12. Earlier comparative glass databases are inherited, not all independently audited.

title: Semi-finished glass from Ile-Ife, Nigeria: implications for the archaeology of glass in sub-Saharan Africa
locator: Accepted manuscript pp. 1–4; sections 2016 and 2017 investigations, Semi-finished glass, Laboratory analysis, Implications and concluding remarks.
scope_limit: Three museum-store fragments recorded from Igbo Olokun, not newly excavated in sealed contexts. Strong primary-production evidence; unique recipe does not by itself exclude transferred ideas or workers.
evidence_lineage: Original examination of three museum-store crucible fragments recorded from Igbo Olokun. Distinct specimens strengthen the same local-production argument as MAT-S12–S13; common site attribution, investigators and interpretive framework limit independence.

title: Questioning Diversity (of Iron) in the Workplace: Bloomery Iron, Cast Iron, China and the West
locator: Internet Archaeology 69; Table 1; sections 2–4, especially cast-iron processing, access to technologies, and concluding social hypotheses. DOI 10.11141/ia.69.14.
scope_limit: Deliberately aggregates China and the West; many dates disputed by its own statement. Cross-craft complements are plausible; broad state-suppression and counterfactual collapse arguments are not accepted here as demonstrated causes.
evidence_lineage: Scholarly synthesis drawing on earlier metallography, excavation literature and Wagner, including evidence related to MAT-S04. The new cross-regional explanation is not a fresh independent set of archaeological observations.

title: The sword that was broken …: The detection of recycled iron in the archaeological record
locator: Archaeometry 65(6):1260–1274; Introduction, Iron production and the forms of iron recycling, illustrative artefacts, Conclusions.
scope_limit: Methods-oriented discussion and selected examples, not representative recycling rates. Composite construction can mimic reuse; documentary and modern ethnographic analogies must not be retrojected automatically.
evidence_lineage: Methods-oriented synthesis combining historical accounts, selected archaeological metallography and authors’ observations. Some examples analysed by authors, others inherited; not a representative survey or independent recycling measurement for the MAT cases.

title: The origins of inoculation
locator: Sections on Ottoman/European inoculation, China and India, and Conclusions; complete article text inspected.
scope_limit: Historical inquiry through reports and older scholarship; early origins, coverage and precise identity/geography of informants remain contested. No reported risk ratio is adopted.
evidence_lineage: Reproduces Timonius, Mather/Onesimus, Pylarinius, North African and other accounts; depends on Needham and earlier historical compilations. Not independent inspection of those original manuscripts. Overlaps the Montagu narrative in MED-S02.

title: Mandating immunity in the Ottoman Empire: A history of public health education and compulsory vaccination
locator: Sections 1–5; full XML body inspected via Europe PMC after PMC browser challenge.
scope_limit: Analysis of official texts and institutional history; prescriptions cannot establish achieved coverage, enforcement frequency or recipients' beliefs.
evidence_lineage: Original scholarly reading of Menafiü’l-Etfal (1846), Ottoman regulations and related historical literature. Those original Ottoman documents were not separately inspected here; reported delivery limits also use cited histories.

title: On the Antiseptic Principle in the Practice of Surgery (1867; 2010 reprint)
locator: 2010 reprint, Clinical Orthopaedics and Related Research 468:2012–2016; clinical body and concluding ward discussion inspected through public HTML retrieval.
scope_limit: Author's clinical advocacy, changing practice and case observations, not a controlled effect estimate; original BMJ scan was located but not separately read.
evidence_lineage: Reprint of Lister's 1867 address; same author and case-report tradition examined by MED-S04 and MED-S05, which are interpretive rereadings rather than independent clinical replications.

title: Joseph Lister and the performance of antiseptic surgery
locator: pp. 199–209; introduction and Antiseptic performance, Surgical performance, Professional performance sections inspected.
scope_limit: Reconstructs practice and communication; does not estimate a diffusion curve or isolate professional incentives quantitatively.
evidence_lineage: Rereads Lister publications/lectures and uses historical work by Crowther, Dupree, Lawrence, Dixey and Schlich. Shares Lister material with MED-S03 and MED-S05.

title: Statistics and the British controversy about the effects of Joseph Lister’s system of antisepsis for surgery, 1867–1890
locator: James Lind Library 2014 version; introduction, case reports, statistics, Glasgow Royal Infirmary and longer-term perspective sections inspected.
scope_limit: The 2014 JLL version is the inspected work, not an assertion of having inspected the later journal edition. Some selection arguments are historians' interpretations.
evidence_lineage: Uses Lister's reports plus Hamilton's reconstruction of Glasgow Royal Infirmary records and other scholarship; Hamilton original not separately inspected. Overlaps MED-S03/S04; comparisons are not independent trials.

title: Watersheds in Child Mortality: The Role of Effective Water and Sewerage Infrastructure, 1880–1920
locator: JPE 127:586–638, corrected reprint; pp. 586–593, introduction to identification/results, Table 4 and robustness discussion pp. 612–614 inspected; appendices not audited in full.
scope_limit: Difference-in-differences for Massachusetts municipalities; Boston excluded from estimation; contingent on rollout exogeneity, mortality registration, interference and model assumptions.
evidence_lineage: Massachusetts vital records, municipal infrastructure histories and state/federal census data; distinct regional design from MED-S07, but historically related water systems/literature. Not independent universal replication of city-level national estimates.

title: Re-Examining the Contribution of Public Health Efforts to the Decline in Urban Mortality (July 2019 manuscript)
locator: July 2019 manuscript; introduction/background, §3 pp. 8–9, §6 pp. 17–18 and conclusion pp. 19–20 inspected.
scope_limit: Working-paper version, not the 2022 final article. Reported estimates and corrections are not independently reproduced. Observational city panel; correlated interventions and denominators matter.
evidence_lineage: Uses US Census Mortality Statistics and Vital Statistics plus intervention histories; reproduces and modifies Cutler–Miller original data/specification. MED-S08 responds within this shared-record dispute; not independent corroborating datasets.

title: Reexamining the Contribution of Public Health Efforts to the Decline in Urban Mortality: Comment
locator: AEA journal abstract and bibliographic record, pp. 158–165; full article not acquired.
scope_limit: Supports only the existence and authors' stated nature of the disagreement, not adjudication or verification of their calculations.
evidence_lineage: Reanalysis of the original Cutler–Miller municipal mortality panel in response to Anderson–Charles–Rees. Shared historical records and disputed coding with MED-S07, not independent replication.

title: Penicillin Production through Deep-tank Fermentation
authors: American Chemical Society, National Historic Chemical Landmarks
locator: The Penicillin Problem; Pfizer’s Growth with Citric Acid and Fermentation; Development of Deep-tank Fermentation; Penicillin Production by Deep-tank Fermentation.
scope_limit: Commemorative institutional/company-centred account; useful process sequence, weak basis for exclusive priority, causal weights, national totals or welfare estimates.
evidence_lineage: ACS landmark account drawing on Pfizer history and materials; detailed archival genealogy not reconstructed. Shares the familiar wartime production narrative with MED-S10, so corroboration is not wholly independent.

title: The Rescue of Penicillin
authors: US Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service
locator: Entire short feature, especially paragraphs on Florey/Heatley visit, culture medium and strain work in 1941–1942.
scope_limit: Institutional retrospective celebrating USDA; no production series or primary laboratory records inspected. Avoid uncorroborated sole-credit language and anecdotes about strain discovery.
evidence_lineage: Institutional history of the Northern Regional Research Laboratory; underlying laboratory notebooks not provided/inspected. Overlaps MED-S09 on transatlantic wartime collaboration.

title: Analysis of Historical Trends and Recent Elimination of Malaria from Sri Lanka and Its Applicability for Malaria Control in Other Countries
locator: Abstract; Malaria in Sri Lanka During the Second Half of the Twentieth Century; Resurgence 1980–2000; Polonnaruwa epidemic sections inspected.
scope_limit: Retrospective mini-review with some authors' own observations; causal labels such as complacency are interpretations. Ancient origins and epidemic totals outside this case are not adopted.
evidence_lineage: Anti-Malaria Campaign historical data and cited government/research accounts plus authors' local research. Overlaps some Sri Lankan narrative/records underlying MED-S12 and institutional account MED-S16.

title: Malaria resurgence: a systematic review and assessment of its causes
locator: Methods; Reported causes of resurgence; Weakening of the malaria control programme; Technical problems; Discussion/limitations.
scope_limit: Counts attributed causes in selected published events; overlapping categories, reporting bias, heterogeneous magnitudes and limited causal evidence. No causal probabilities inferred.
evidence_lineage: Original systematic review of 208 reports describing 75 events; a secondary synthesis of individual outbreaks. Its Sri Lanka subcase overlaps source traditions in MED-S11 rather than adding independent observations.

title: Magic bullet: the history of oral rehydration therapy
locator: Medical History 38:363–397; methodological introduction pp. 363–365 and implementation/interpretation pp. 389–393 inspected in parsed PDF.
scope_limit: Retrospective interviews with scientific participants; claims of unique discovery, priority and entire medical profession's motives not taken as settled. Not a complete clinical-trial audit.
evidence_lineage: Original oral-history interviews and contemporary research articles. Ruxin cites Nalin, Cash, Mahalanabis and other investigators; scientific participants also appear in MED-S14, producing partly shared insider perspectives.

title: The status of ORT in Bangladesh: how widely is it used?
locator: Health Policy and Planning 12:58–66; methods, Box 1, Tables 1–3, Discussion pp. 64–65. Full public text and publisher PDF parsed tables inspected; no page-by-page visual audit.
scope_limit: 1993 survey of 90 villages in BRAC programme cohorts, two-week recalled episodes; broad ORT measure includes home fluids. Abstract and Table 2 differ; no randomized programme-effect identification.
evidence_lineage: Original household/provider/shop survey and chemical testing of 269 prepared solutions; investigators include programme personnel. Earlier programme reach and comparison rates inherited from earlier BRAC studies not independently inspected.
