title: Addressing Antibiotic Abuse in China: An Experimental Audit Study
locator: J Dev Econ 110:39–51, author manuscript; §§I–IV, especially §III study design and experiment scripts, plus stated results and limitations inspected.
scope_limit: One unnamed large city, October 2011–June 2012; young healthy standardized patients; encounter prescribing, not resistance outcomes or system-wide reform. Auditors knew study purpose.
evidence_lineage: Original two audit experiments: 320 visits/80 physicians then 300 visits/120 physicians; randomly assigned roles and ordering. Discussion also cites earlier audits, which are not counted as separately inspected evidence.

title: Address by Regional Director on the occasion of Malaria Elimination Certification by the Government of Sri Lanka
authors: WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia
locator: 30 November 2016 speech; certification announcement paragraph and first six listed institutional factors inspected.
scope_limit: Contemporaneous official certification account, also celebratory; causal explanation is institutional interpretation, not controlled evaluation. No current status claim is made.
evidence_lineage: WHO certification and Sri Lankan programme reporting; specific underlying certification dossier not inspected. Shares programme history with MED-S11; independent public confirmation of the dated announcement, not independent incidence measurement.

title: ORBIS: The Stanford Geospatial Network Model of the Roman World, version dated 2 May 2012
locator: PDF acquired and text extracted. Inspected pp. 7–11 (expectations, coverage, seasonality), 17 (price calibration), 18–19 (road coverage and chronology).
scope_limit: Historical network model, not observed traffic or diffusion. Selected Roman-era features treated as contemporaneous; partly calibrated from the 301 CE price edict. Does not cover the Red Sea/Indian Ocean in this version. Stanford download worked although browser text fetch failed.
evidence_lineage: Model draws on Barrington Atlas and ancient route evidence, the 301 CE price edict and modern/experimental transport parameters; historical inputs overlap older Roman transport-cost scholarship. This contribution does not independently reread every ancient source.

title: The costs of transporting goods by different modes: A case study of pottery movement in late Roman Britain
locator: Journal of Archaeological Science 170, 106059; DOI 10.1016/j.jas.2024.106059. Inspected abstract, §1.1, Table 3, §§4.4–5, pp. 1–2 and 8–10. Full PDF acquired.
scope_limit: Pottery distribution in lowland Britain c. 250–400 CE, predominantly rural settlements; sparse large towns and little military transport. Inferred cost ratios depend on demand/cost and network assumptions; cannot be transferred to all Roman freight.
evidence_lineage: Original analysis of archaeological pottery distributions and a reconstructed transport network; interprets and challenges the price-edict/ORBIS tradition in MOB-S01. Independent material evidence partly contrasts with, but does not make its model assumptions independent of, that tradition.

title: Qhapaq Ñan, Andean Road System (No. 1459): ICOMOS advisory body evaluation
locator: Report approved 7 March 2014; printed pp. 320–342. Inspected pp. 321–325 (components, history) and 327–328 (authenticity and maintenance) in web-extracted PDF full text.
scope_limit: Heritage evaluation based on nominated segments, missions and supplied documentation. Not a traffic census or neutral estimate of imperial welfare; some historical formulations are broad and celebratory. Do not equate nominated road length with total original network length.
evidence_lineage: ICOMOS evaluation of six states’ nomination, supplementary inventories and 2013 technical missions. Inherits modern Andean historiography and selected archaeological evidence; not independent corroboration of every chronicler claim.

title: Rethinking imperial infrastructure: A bottom-up perspective on the Inca Road
locator: Journal of Anthropological Archaeology 43, 94–109; DOI 10.1016/j.jaa.2016.06.001. Author-posted full-text OCR inspected, especially §§2.1, 4.1–4.4, 5 and 6, pp. 95–106.
scope_limit: Full-coverage survey of 58 square kilometres and a 12 km road segment, plus selected excavations, in Cachiyuyo de Llampos, Atacama. Local economic autonomy is an archaeological interpretation; absence of elite architecture is not direct proof of absence of imperial control. OCR interleaves some columns; no unverified table values used.
evidence_lineage: Author’s 2014 full-coverage survey, surface recording and selected test pits/AMS samples, combined with earlier surveys and post-conquest chroniclers. Direct archaeological contribution is distinct from inherited Hyslop/D’Altroy descriptions; those originals were not separately inspected.

title: Railroads of the Raj: Estimating the Impact of Transportation Infrastructure
locator: American Economic Review 108(4–5), 899–934, DOI 10.1257/aer.20101199. Published PDF acquired; inspected §§I.B–C (pp. 904–907), V (pp. 922–928), Table 4 and conclusion.
scope_limit: District agricultural output/income and trade, largely 1870–1930; not comprehensive household welfare. Nonrandom placement addressed with historical plans/placebos and model discipline, not randomized assignment. Published 2018 version used, not the 2008 job-market draft.
evidence_lineage: Original assembly and econometric analysis of colonial district crop/output, price, trade, rainfall and railway/planning records; model uses additional assumptions. Historical planning account inherits Thorner/Macpherson/Headrick. Does not independently corroborate company employment data in MOB-S06.

title: Regulation, Ownership and Costs: A Historical Perspective from Indian Railways, April 2011 version
locator: Complete author manuscript acquired. Inspected §§1–2, pp. 6–8 (guarantees and purchase clauses), quality discussion, pp. 22–25 and Tables 7–9 (expense and employment mechanisms).
scope_limit: This is the April 2011 manuscript, preceding the 2012 AEJ: Economic Policy publication. It reports about 14% lower expenses; this contribution uses the qualitative result rather than conflating editions. Wages/salaries directly unavailable; lower employment supports the labour-cost mechanism.
evidence_lineage: Original railway-system panel from Administration Reports and related Government of India sources, with wage proxies and contract/ownership histories. Some institutional narrative and scholars overlap MOB-S05/MOB-S07. April 2011 manuscript must not be silently equated to 2012 publication.

title: Extractive institutions? Investor returns to Indian railway companies in the age of high imperialism, April 2019 accepted manuscript
locator: Full author manuscript acquired, internally dated April 2019 despite March filename. Inspected pp. 1–3, guaranteed-security return definitions and Table 2a. Published in Journal of Institutional Economics 15(5), 751–774, DOI 10.1017/S1744137419000237.
scope_limit: Returns to listed securities are not the same as the entire colonial resource transfer or social return. Series span wider dates, but the 3.7% figure used here concerns guaranteed securities during 1880–1908. The full accepted manuscript, not merely publisher abstract, supports the claim.
evidence_lineage: Original calculations from Investors Monthly Manual securities data, using the Yale ICF digitization and historical company/ownership classifications. Financial data differ from MOB-S06 operating accounts, but same authors and institutional interpretation create nonindependence.

title: The Permanent Effects of Transportation Revolutions in Poor Countries: Evidence from Africa, January 2015 forthcoming version
locator: Full PDF accessible through web text; inspected introduction, §§2–4 and selected §5–6 passages, especially printed pp. 5–9, 14–15, 22–25 and Table 3. Subsequent publication: Review of Economics and Statistics 98(2), 268–284 (2016).
scope_limit: Use this version explicitly. Main Ghana analysis uses 0.1-degree grid cells and census data 1891–2000; wider African comparisons are secondary here. Rail location is not random; planned lines and instruments reduce rather than eliminate selection concerns. Historical labour/forest descriptions cite earlier scholarship not separately inspected.
evidence_lineage: Original historical GIS and census/cocoa dataset combined with colonial railway histories and planned routes. Ghana findings and wider African checks share methods and authors. Maintenance, labour and forest narratives inherit Luntinen, Hill, Ruf and other scholarship, not separately inspected originals.

title: The Electric Car and the Burden of History: Studies in Automotive Systems Rivalry in America, 1890–1996
locator: Business and Economic History 26(2), 304–310. Full seven-page dissertation summary acquired; inspected pp. 304–310, especially EVC pp. 306–307 and EVAA pp. 308–309.
scope_limit: Author summary of archival dissertation, not the dissertation itself. Initial profitability uses later cost estimates; hypothetical successful EVC and earlier utility coordination are explicit counterfactuals. Historical discussion only; its 1990s forecasts are excluded.
evidence_lineage: Author’s compressed presentation of his 1996 archival dissertation; early EVC reports and later cost studies underlie the operational assessment. Counterfactual argument belongs to the author. MOB-S10 cites Kirsch and shares the failed-technology debate, so agreement is not fully independent.

title: Das Scheitern des frühen Elektromobils (1895–1925): Versuch einer Neubewertung
locator: Technikgeschichte 64(4), 269–285. Complete German PDF acquired; inspected overview, pp. 269–271, pp. 281–283 (conclusions), and explanatory notes pp. 283–285. Paraphrases translated during research.
scope_limit: Archival research synthesis disaggregates periods, Europe/US and vehicle tasks. Many primary citations abbreviated into companion dissertation. Some claims about cultural transfer are interpretive; no universal battery-range or market-share claim used.
evidence_lineage: Author’s archival dissertation research in Europe and America summarized in a German article, with many original citations deferred to the book/dissertation. Explicitly cites Kirsch’s dissertation; distinct fleet evidence coexists with a connected interpretive lineage.

title: Estimating the effects of the container revolution on world trade
locator: Published Journal of International Economics 98, 36–50, DOI 10.1016/j.jinteco.2015.09.001. Full PDF acquired; inspected pp. 36–40, Tables 2–3, pp. 44–47 and Appendix Table 1.
scope_limit: Published article, not 2012–2014 working papers. Authors explicitly reject confident causal interpretation of adoption-timing estimates where parallel trends fail; product comparisons are smaller and depend on classification. Historical standardization/military narrative draws on prior histories, particularly Levinson, not independently inspected archives.
evidence_lineage: Original trade/adoption dataset assembled from Containerisation International, trade records and engineering classifications. Historical narrative inherits Levinson, McKinsey and other accounts. Published 2016 estimates and warnings supersede claims from earlier drafts; those drafts are not separate corroboration.

title: Volkswagenwerk Aktiengesellschaft v. Federal Maritime Commission, 390 U.S. 261
authors: Supreme Court of the United States
locator: Decision 6 March 1968. Full opinion available; inspected opening paragraphs 1–9, especially paragraphs 2–4, and discussion of assessment arrangements.
scope_limit: Judicial record of a dispute over financing the West Coast mechanization fund. Direct evidence of agreement and litigated incidence, not an evaluation of all workers or proof that compensation equalled losses. Used historically, not as current legal advice.
evidence_lineage: 1968 Supreme Court opinion recounting the 1960 agreement, fund and assessment dispute from litigation. Primary judicial record; not the signed contract itself and not a census of all labour effects. Same historical settlement appears in MOB-S13.

title: California Cartage Co. v. NLRB, 822 F.2d 1203
authors: United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit
locator: Decision 14 July 1987. Full opinion available; inspected opening procedural account and part I, paragraphs on the 1960 M&M agreement and off-dock stuffing/unstuffing.
scope_limit: Retrospective judicial account of Board findings and competing parties, focusing on work jurisdiction. Its descriptions of restrictive practices are the court’s characterization. Does not measure economy-wide job losses or establish a comprehensive welfare balance.
evidence_lineage: 1987 appellate opinion recounting NLRB decisions and a 1971 dispute about the 1969/1970 work-jurisdiction supplement. Same M&M settlement as MOB-S12, with distinct later dispute evidence; two judicial accounts do not constitute two independent labour-impact studies.

title: Speech by Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong at the opening of the Pasir Panjang Terminal, 30 March 2000
locator: National Archives of Singapore press-release PDF, 4 pages. Inspected paragraphs 1–6, especially paragraph 3 (1972 berths), paragraphs 4–5 (land, planning and complements).
scope_limit: Official self-presentation at a terminal opening; primary evidence of government rationale and retrospective chronology, not an independent causal evaluation. Do not infer residents’ consent, complete land costs or actual realized future capacity from the speech.
evidence_lineage: Contemporary 2000 government press release of a terminal-opening speech, retrospectively describing 1972 and subsequent planning. Primary evidence of the official account and stated rationale; underlying port records and residents’ accounts were not independently inspected.

title: Papermaking: The Historical Diffusion of an Ancient Technique
locator: Mobilities of Knowledge, chapter 3, pp. 51–66; inspected pp. 51–64, especially 52–54 and 63–64; full text also inspected in ResearchGate PDF mirror.
scope_limit: Comparative survey with some conjectural transmission and preference explanations. The underlying medieval documents were not independently inspected. No precise first, Talas explanation, India/West Africa preference claim, or universal hydraulic-mill lineage is adopted.
evidence_lineage: Synthesises the author's Paper Before Print (2001), not directly read here, and earlier scholarship. Tunis watermark evidence is inherited from Valls i Subirà (1970); the Ibn Marzuq ruling from Halevi (2008) and Lagardère (1995). The European paper-property discussion draws on Barrett, also NET-S02, so these are not independent corroborations.

title: European Papermaking Techniques 1300–1800
locator: University of Iowa, Paper Through Time; dated August 2011; inspected Introduction, Raw Materials/Water, and Sizing.
scope_limit: Author explicitly calls parts of this a generalisation and hypothesis from limited early records, later craft descriptions and practical experience; not a census of historical mills or a measured adoption series.
evidence_lineage: Reworks Barrett's 1989 essay and combines historical-paper research, personal papermaking experience, and eighteenth-century descriptions by Lalande, Goussier and Desmarest. Shared material foundation with Bloom NET-S01; not a separate medieval documentary sample.

title: Material properties of Islamic paper
locator: Heritage Science 4:34, DOI 10.1186/s40494-016-0103-4; inspected pp. 1–3, 9–10 and collection/method limitations.
scope_limit: 228-paper conservation reference collection; 133 undated; most dated samples much later than medieval diffusion. Abstract and methods describe chronology differently. Unknown provenance/storage limits inference; used to bound attribution, not measure medieval uptake.
evidence_lineage: Original laboratory analyses of a UCL reference collection; the same physical papers underpin all reported analytical methods. Independent material research but not an independent medieval chronology. Historical background draws on earlier codicological literature.

title: A Selection of Shen Gua's Writings in Translation, appendix 3 to Shen Gua's Empiricism
locator: Appendix pp. 22–24, section on movable-type printing, with notes 67–71; original Brush Talks from Dream Brook, late eleventh century, describing 1041–1048.
scope_limit: Historical testimony in a modern scholarly translation. Described efficiency is Shen's assessment, not a modern replication result. The main 2018 book was not inspected. Translator's clay-composition debate is not adjudicated here.
evidence_lineage: Translation of Shen's Mengxi bitan passage with Chinese text and modern annotation. This is the same frequently cited historical account underlying many claims about Bi Sheng; repetition by later historians is not independent eyewitness corroboration.

title: Introduction, The Book Worlds of East Asia and Europe, 1450–1850: Connections and Comparisons
locator: Publisher preview includes introduction pp. 1–64; inspected pp. 11–15 and 17–24, with references and relevant figures' captions.
scope_limit: Selected chapter pages, not entire edited book. Comparative cost statements are qualitative and heterogeneous across periods. Some early European type-casting details and transfer claims are disputed. No uniform cross-civilisation cost ratio is inferred.
evidence_lineage: Technology/workflow comparison synthesises McDermott (2006), Chia, Brokaw, Chow, Tsien, Gaskell and others. Ricci's cost remark is inherited testimony, not an independent price series. Chinese movable-type origin ultimately overlaps NET-S04. Much European production history also overlaps sources inherited by NET-S09/S10.

title: Buddhist texts: The Diamond Sutra
locator: Sections The Diamond Sutra, How and why was it made?, and Colophon from the Diamond Sutra; object Or.8210/P.2, dated 11 May 868.
scope_limit: Custodian's object description and translated colophon inspected; no independent material examination or original-Chinese collation. Earliest-dated-survivor language does not identify invention or actual distribution volume.
evidence_lineage: The physical scroll and its colophon are the underlying record. This institutional page and other Diamond Sutra webpages describe the same object and are not independent witnesses to diffusion.

title: Jikji, a treasure of the world of printing
locator: Sections What is Jikji?, A treasure of humanity, From Korea to France, and Preservation and access; BnF Coréen 109.
scope_limit: Custodian description of a surviving second volume and a 1378 xylograph counterpart. Does not establish print-run size, commercial success, widespread literacy or the earliest-ever use of metal type.
evidence_lineage: Underlying surviving 1377 Jikji volume/colophon and Korean 1378 woodblock edition. UNESCO recognition is not an independent experiment; Park's mention of Jikji in NET-S08 refers to the same artifact tradition.

title: Manuscript, Not Print, in the Book World of Chosŏn Korea (1392–1910)
locator: The Routledge Companion to Korean Literature, chapter 1, pp. 19–38; inspected pp. 19–28 and conclusion pp. 34–35, especially pp. 22–27 and p. 27 n. 16.
scope_limit: Selected full chapter within a publisher preview, not entire volume. Combines historiographical critique and case-based manuscript research; no representative readership, literacy or wage series. Later examples are identified as subepisodes, not evidence for fourteenth-century diffusion.
evidence_lineage: Re-examines Courant's Korean Bibliography and scholarship on surviving vernacular and literary manuscripts. Rental chronology relies on earlier studies and literati accounts; state/private examples cite Walraven (2007) and No (2013), not directly read here. Comparative framing partly draws on NET-S05 and shared book-history literature.

title: Information Technology and Economic Change: The Impact of the Printing Press
locator: Quarterly Journal of Economics 126:1133–1172, DOI 10.1093/qje/qjr035; inspected pp. 1133–44, 1153–56 and §V.E (pp. 1157 onward), especially Table I and nn. 20–23, 38, 40.
scope_limit: City-level historical data and conditional instrumental-variable design, not national productivity or welfare. Table I's historical-city denominator differs from regression samples. Some production-history details are inherited and contested; mature casting should not be projected intact into 1450.
evidence_lineage: Adoption compilation combines ISTC (1998), Febvre and Martin (1958), Clair (1976); populations from Bairoch, Batou and Chèvre (1988). The 205-city list and 27,873 edition records are not separate independent uptake samples. Shared historical foundations and arguments recur in NET-S10.

title: New Media and Competition: Printing and Europe's Transformation after Gutenberg
locator: CEP Discussion Paper 1600, January 2019; inspected pp. 1–7, §3.1 and price/competition and identification discussions in §§5–7; p. 3 summarises price results.
scope_limit: Working-paper version, not assumed identical to later publication. Introduction reports over 295,000 publications; §3.1 over 299,000 editions. Edition counts are not copies, sales or readers; prices have a separate selected purchasing-record sample. Exclusion restrictions require scrutiny.
evidence_lineage: USTC 2012 editions; Hoock/Jeannin merchants' manuals; Hernando Colón purchase records; printer biographies including Reske; publications naming heirs/widows. Distinct evidence layers but not independent replications of one causal result. Reuses NET-S09's adoption history/cost account; printer-death measures have different survival selection.

title: Did Ottoman Sultans Ban Print?
locator: Book History 20:1–39, DOI 10.1353/bh.2017.0000; inspected pp. 1–11, 16–20, 22–29 and associated notes; documentary core pp. 6–11.
scope_limit: No surviving general ban is not proof of no restriction. Interpretation is scoped to the alleged Bayezid/Selim bans and extant 1588/1727 documents. Original Ottoman documents not independently read; translations and close reading are Schwartz's.
evidence_lineage: Traces inherited ban claims through Thevet, Guignes, Cheikho and Lewis, so their repeated assertion is one transmission chain. Documentary counterevidence is the 1588 firman reproduced in a 1594 Euclid and Müteferrika's 1729 prefatory firman/fatwa materials. Uses Sabev critically; not an independent archive of his probate quantities.

title: Formation of Ottoman Print Culture (1726–1746): Some General Remarks
locator: New Europe College Regional Program 2003–2004, 2004–2005, pp. 293–333; inspected pp. 293, 299–307 and relevant notes.
scope_limit: Uses sixteen-edition grouping; appendices/titles need not equal other catalogues' counts. Three print runs estimated. Stock depletion is not observed sales; gifts and unequal time on market matter. Probate reader sample restricted to Istanbul askeri decedents with more than three books, not population literacy.
evidence_lineage: Original research on Müteferrika's probate inventory and selected Istanbul Askeriye probate registers, plus initial-run statements and contemporary observers. Later percentage claims often recycle this one estate reconstruction. This contribution did not inspect the original register or count its entries independently.

title: Indian Ocean navigation in Islamic sources 850–1560 CE
locator: History Compass 16:e12485, DOI 10.1111/hic3.12485; author-uploaded full-text extraction inspected, especially §§2–4, pp. 2–7.
scope_limit: Primarily Arabic/Turkish textual corpus, not representative of all Indian Ocean crews. Chronology of surviving detailed texts is not invention chronology. No instrument-carriage or accident denominator. Do not use incidental ancient-compass or first-crossing claims.
evidence_lineage: Synthesis of Ibn Majid, al-Mahri and Sidi Ali Reis through editions/translations, especially Tibbetts and Khoury, plus Portuguese testimony. Shares core manuscript corpus with NET-S14 and partly the voyage tradition of NET-S15. Translation bias and neglect of Arabic editions are explicitly discussed.

title: Reflections on the Knowledge of Shallow Waters
locator: Isis 112(1), DOI 10.1086/713561; full HTML essay inspected; especially paragraphs beginning It appears that early Portuguese sailors, Curiously, and Where the Chinese compass.
scope_limit: Comparative reflection, not a measured compass-carriage survey. Its generalisation that the Islamic world resisted print is excluded in light of NET-S11. Potential naming/conflation issues in its compressed navigation genealogy are not used.
evidence_lineage: Uses Ibn Majid via Tibbetts and the author's prior maritime research, overlapping NET-S13's core texts. Chinese comparisons depend on Papelitzky's separate essay, not inspected here. Agreement on navigational practices is therefore not two independent fleet samples.

title: A Journal of the First Voyage of Vasco da Gama, 1497–1499
locator: Hakluyt Society translation, public-domain electronic transcription; inspected voyage narrative pp. 40–47, especially 45–47 (Malindi, 22–24 April 1498 and Arabian Sea crossing).
scope_limit: Translation of a surviving manuscript tradition, not an unmediated modern log. Anonymous attribution and editorial brackets are retained as such. Christian identifications are unreliable for religion/ethnicity; no identification of the pilot with Ibn Majid is made. One episode cannot measure fleet-level dependence.
evidence_lineage: Anonymous Roteiro narrative mediated by Ravenstein's nineteenth-century edition. Staples discusses the same voyage tradition, so this checks the narrated episode directly in translation but is not an independent second voyage. Editorial notes are distinguished from the historical narrator.

title: Hokule‘a 1980 (reprinted in “A Journey by the Stars”)
authors: Will Kyselka; introduced by Cecil Heftel
locator: Congressional Record, 17 September 1980, Extensions of Remarks, p. 25908; original Ka ‘Elele, July 1980. Only the Kyselka item and introduction inspected, not unrelated remarks.
scope_limit: Participant account, not independent performance audit. The congressional introduction oversimplifies navigation as entirely by stars; the reproduced account describes several cues, planetarium training, escort communication and comparison with instrument fixes.
evidence_lineage: Contemporaneous participant account republished verbatim from the Bishop Museum newsletter; congressional republication is not independent corroboration. Raw fix logs and original newsletter not acquired.

title: History: The Story of Hōkūle‘a
locator: Sections The Story of Hōkūle‘a, first voyage, tragedy, A Generation of Renewal, Master Navigators.
scope_limit: Community institution’s retrospective public history; commemorative claims about whole-population identity, last voyages and causal effects on all Hawaiian culture are not adopted here.
evidence_lineage: PVS participant memories and institutional narrative; overlaps the same voyages and network as S01 and S03. Exact archival bases of every statement not supplied.

title: Hōkūleʻa Mo‘olelo: The Pwo Ceremony
locator: 17 March 2017 post; first-person account of March 2007 Satawal visit and initiation; final adaptation note.
scope_limit: Eyewitness ceremony account adapted a decade later from Hawaiki Rising. Use March 2007 rather than exact ceremony day because S02 gives 18 March and this post gives 17 March. Heroic claims and unrelated political chronology are not used.
evidence_lineage: Sam Low’s witnessed ceremony and his own book, republished by PVS. S02 and S03 are one institutional lineage, not independent evidence for broader cultural impact.

title: Dating Aboriginal stone-walled fishtraps at Lake Condah, southeast Australia
authors: Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners Aboriginal Corporation
locator: Journal of Archaeological Science 39:268–286; article text inspected via https://www.academia.edu/16379574/Dating_Aboriginal_stone_walled_fishtraps_at_Lake_Condah_southeast_Australia ; especially pp.268–272, 279–284, sections 3.9 and 4.
scope_limit: HTML extraction of article sections, not downloaded publisher PDF. Sediment-charcoal ages and stratigraphy constrain one feature’s history; stone itself was not radiocarbon dated; no regional adoption rate.
evidence_lineage: Original partnership excavations at Muldoons Trap Complex, channel F10, sediment analyses and 16 AMS dates; later nomination S05 inherits this chronology rather than independently reproducing it.

title: Budj Bim Cultural Landscape: World Heritage Nomination
authors: Commonwealth of Australia, Department of the Environment and Energy; developed with Gunditjmara Traditional Owners
locator: December 2017 dossier: front matter; Part 2B, especially pp.68–70 on drainage and restoration; pp.18–21 and 36–40 on system and chronology. Selected sections inspected.
scope_limit: Nomination is a selective argument for heritage recognition. Colonial observations and older scholarship are mediated citations unless separately inspected. Use local engineered-water outcomes, not oldest/continuous/universal welfare superlatives.
evidence_lineage: Combines Gunditjmara testimony and custodial knowledge, archaeological work including S04, earlier histories and restoration feasibility/management records. The latter reports were referenced but not independently acquired; shares community project lineage with S06.

title: Lake Condah Restoration Project
authors: Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners Aboriginal Corporation
locator: Project page, paragraphs on 1954 drain, failed trial, 2004 plan, 2006 studies, March 2008 return and January–May 2010 construction; employment bullets.
scope_limit: Direct implementing institution’s account, not independent labour evaluation. No worker count, wage series, retention or household income distribution. Page undated; inspected 5 November 2026.
evidence_lineage: Gunditj Mirring account of its restoration programme and partners, including funding, tendering and training; substantially same project history reused in S05.

title: The “fire stick farming” hypothesis: Australian Aboriginal foraging strategies, biodiversity, and anthropogenic fire mosaics
locator: PNAS 105:14796–14801; PDF https://web.stanford.edu/~jhj1/papers/bird_etal2008.pdf ; Ethnoecological Context, three Results tests, Discussion, Materials and Methods.
scope_limit: Observed contemporary Martu hunts and landscape comparisons, not randomized burning assignments; broad ancient-Australia claims exceed study. Species diversity is not identical to successional patch diversity.
evidence_lineage: Original 2002 field observations (1,095 forager-hours, 421 bouts, 59 camp-days), 34 landscape circles and Landsat classification; some hunting results reprise team’s previous field publications. Overlaps study programme and population with S08.

title: Aboriginal hunting buffers climate-driven fire-size variability in Australia’s spinifex grasslands
locator: PNAS 109:10287–10292; Results, Tables 1–2, Discussion, Materials and Methods.
scope_limit: Regimes classified by proximity to communities/tracks, not ignition observation of every fire; nonrandom spatial comparison; contemporary regional study. Mammal-population benefit is proposed, not directly measured here.
evidence_lineage: Original 1999–2010 Landsat sequence and 2000–2010 foraging observations (347 sample days, 1,811 bouts, 104 foragers); extends and partly overlaps S07, rather than independent replication.

title: Origins of Agriculture at Kuk Swamp in the Highlands of New Guinea
locator: Science 301:189–193; acquired https://faculty.washington.edu/plape/pacificarchaut12/Denham%20et%20al%202003.pdf ; Site and stratigraphy, Archaeological evidence, Table 1.
scope_limit: Original article acquired; supporting online material not separately inspected. Cultivation inference combines proxies. Earliest phase and global independent-invention conclusion require more evidence than the dates alone.
evidence_lineage: Renewed Kuk excavations, sediment sequence, radiocarbon dates, pollen/phytolith/starch and other proxies, interpreting earlier Kuk research. S10 revisits shared site and evidence, not a fully independent confirmation.

title: Phase 3: The Emergence of Ditches
locator: In Ten Thousand Years of Cultivation at Kuk Swamp, Terra Australis 46, pp.221–237, DOI 10.22459/TA46.07.2017.13; especially pp.224–225, 234–237.
scope_limit: Kuk is better investigated than comparator valleys; reconstructions of property, risk and causes of abandonment are explicit hypotheses, not recovered institutions or recorded decisions.
evidence_lineage: Excavation records and ditch plans from Kuk, with published records from Warrawau, Kana, Tambul and Haeapugua. Shared Kuk lineage with S09; some other-site evidence is mediated through earlier reports.

title: Experimental Growing of Pre-European Cultivars of Kūmara (Sweet Potato, Ipomoea batatas [L.] Lam.) at the Southern Margins of Māori Horticulture
locator: NZ Journal of Archaeology 23 (2001), published 2003, pp.161–188; text inspected via https://www.academia.edu/111593238/Experimental_growing_of_pre_European_cultivators_of_kumara_sweet_potato_Ipomoea_Batatas_L_Lam_at_the_southern_margins_of_Maori_horticulture ; pp.162–173,177–185.
scope_limit: Initial NZAA parameterized PDF redirected to an unrelated fishing paper; rejected and documented. Correct article verified by title, authors and page footer in HTML mirror. Modern climate, virus-treated collection stock, fencing/windbreak and unreplicated plots; traditional storage not replicated.
evidence_lineage: Original gardens at Robin Hood Bay and Whatarangi, starting 1999/2000; inherited cultivar collection assembled by Yen in 1955–1958 and later repatriated and treated. Cultivar authenticity assessed morphologically, not proof of unchanged ancient yield potential.

title: Research at the interface between Indigenous knowledge and soil science; weaving knowledges to understand horticultural land use in Aotearoa / New Zealand
scope_limit: Pōhatu site and two soil profiles; specific amendment identifications and temporal interpretations remain uncertain. Research supports restoration goals but does not establish a new garden’s adoption, commercial viability or employment effects.
evidence_lineage: Original collaborative soil investigation and Mana Whenua interpretation; place names, waiata and manuscripts mediated partly through coauthor Payne’s 2020 research; contemporary geochemistry and microbotany. Historical deed narrative cites Evison, not inspected original deed.

title: American sweet potato and Asia-Pacific crop experimentation during early colonisation of temperate-climate Aotearoa/New Zealand
locator: Antiquity 98(401):1376–1394; Cambridge HTML and PDF extraction, especially Results, Table 1/Figure 10 and Discussion pp.1383–1391; https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/antiquity/article/american-sweet-potato-and-asiapacific-crop-experimentation-during-early-colonisation-of-temperateclimate-aotearoanew-zealand/B6446CB196635B1CDB44DC7506F696C8 .
scope_limit: Article text inspected; supplementary reference granule atlas and full model not independently reanalysed. Morphological starch assignments are probabilistic; absence of taro/yam in later samples does not prove cultural disappearance across Te Waipounamu.
evidence_lineage: New starch/palynomorph analysis and radiocarbon modelling at M24/11 using earlier excavation contexts; some site interpretation inherits Barber’s prior reports. Separate material from Pōhatu and Cook Strait trials.

title: He Pukoa Kani ‘Āina: Kanaka Maoli approaches to mo‘okū‘auhau as methodology
locator: AlterNative 8(2):137–147; PDF text inspected, especially pp.142–145 on interviews, volunteering, Shantell Ching and other women’s accounts. Filename ends 143 but article continues to 147.
scope_limit: Methodological article excerpting purposive interviews and researcher experience; not representative survey, wage study or proof of supernatural/biological mechanisms. Accounted beliefs are evidence of meaning, not independently verified physical explanations.
evidence_lineage: Author’s original interviews and participant experience, drawing on her 2010 doctoral thesis. This is a distinct research collection, while interviewees belong to the same voyaging network as S01–S03; full thesis not inspected.

title: Giving Up the Gun? Overcoming Myths about Japanese Sword-Hunting and Firearms Control
locator: History of Global Arms Transfer 6, pp. 45–59; especially II, pp. 50–53, notes 52–83
scope_limit: Historical reassessment, not an original national firearm census; numerical examples inherited from Japanese historians. Modern gun-policy implications are outside this contribution.
evidence_lineage: Reviews Fujiki Hisashi, Takei Kōichi, Tsukamoto Manabu, and Howell. Shiiba/Matsumoto counts cited through Fujiki, not newly counted here. Not independent corroboration of Howell.
inspection_detail: Full PDF cached; sections I–III and relevant notes read. Raw local PDF and extracted text preserved.

title: The Social Life of Firearms in Tokugawa Japan
locator: Japanese Studies 29(1), pp. 65–80; publisher abstract and visible notes
scope_limit: Only abstract and notes available through indexed publisher text; live full-text request returned 403. No claim of reading its case narratives or archives.
evidence_lineage: Author identifies Tsukamoto Manabu as a basis; focuses on Edo hinterland institutions. Enomoto and Noordam also inherit this work. Full evidentiary genealogy not inspected.
inspection_detail: Read the complete publisher abstract and visible notes in search response; author page explicitly says no PDF posted for copyright reasons. 1840s interpretation remains provisional.

title: Introduction: the reception of the harquebus in East and South-East Asia
locator: International Journal of Asian Studies, First View, pp. 1–18; Japan section, especially p. 9
scope_limit: State-of-field introduction; accounts of Galindo and Howell are inherited summaries. Do not convert the review into independent archival evidence or a national gun-ownership estimate.
evidence_lineage: Synthesis of regional scholarship and special-issue contributions; Japan section explicitly draws on Galindo and Howell, overlapping S02 and S01.
inspection_detail: Full HTML available and relevant introduction/Japan section inspected; local PDF download failed 403. Published online 27 July 2026, not 2025 as initially guessed from search timing.

title: The rise and fall of paper money in Yuan China, 1260–1368
locator: Accepted manuscript, pp. 10–18, 19–28, 38–57; Tables 1–5; Figure 6; published DOI 10.1111/ehr.13305
scope_limit: Accepted version, not final typeset article. CPI uses sparse prices and interpolation; monetary stock assumes annual attrition. Time-series associations are not exogenous causal identification; no endorsement of inevitable failure.
evidence_lineage: New assembled series from Yuanshi, Yuandianzhang and other printed records; commodity prices inherited from Li; wars/disasters from Chen et al.; draws on Peng, von Glahn and Vogel. Regressions share these reconstructed series.
inspection_detail: Full 82-page PDF acquired; main historical, data and regression sections plus relevant tables read. Not a replication of the raw data or a new reading of original Chinese records.

title: The distinctive uses of two monetary units, guanwen and dingliang, in Yuan China (1260–1368) as recorded in 'Heicheng chutuwenshu' and 'Huizhou qiyuewenshu'
locator: Socio-Economic History 68(3), pp. 249–270; English abstract
scope_limit: Only English abstract inspected; cannot audit individual contracts, their dates, sample sizes or readings.
evidence_lineage: Original scholarship reports analysis of Heicheng excavated documents and Huizhou contracts, a different evidentiary route from aggregate official money series; original documents not inspected here.
inspection_detail: Read abstract on J-STAGE, DOI 10.20624/sehs.68.3_249. Japanese full text not acquired or claimed read.

title: The Book of Ser Marco Polo, Book II, Part I, Chapter XXIV: paper currency
locator: Columbia Asia for Educators, two-page excerpt from 1903 Yule edition; especially p. 2
scope_limit: Late-thirteenth-century travel narrative in a later translation, with rhetorical claims of universal acceptance and inexhaustible wealth; not an acceptance survey or enforcement register.
evidence_lineage: Medieval Polo narrative mediated by manuscript/translation history; Columbia reproduces the Yule edition. Modern monetary historians also cite Polo, so partial overlap is possible.
inspection_detail: Both excerpt pages read and cached. No construction/manufacturing instructions used in the report.

title: Communication Infrastructure and Stabilizing Food Prices: Evidence from the Telegraph Network in China
locator: AEA-hosted accepted manuscript, sections I–V; pp. 6–17 and 22–29; Tables 3, 6–7; published DOI 10.1257/app.20190416
scope_limit: Panel covers 130 prefectures in nine provinces, 1870–1904; treatment is office access, not usage intensity. Timing/parallel-trend and reporting assumptions remain; manuscript contains prose inconsistencies.
evidence_lineage: Qing Grain Price Database from provincial reports; routes from Chinese Customs 1907 postal map, dates from Wang 1988 and local gazetteers; weather from historical compendium. Institutional narrative inherits Baark and Yoon.
inspection_detail: Full PDF cached; background, data construction, baseline/event study, robustness, weather interactions and volatility sections inspected. No re-estimation or staggered-DID reanalysis. Uses explicit 64/130 and 147/299 counts, not inconsistent 40% prose.

title: Dashed Expectations: Limitations of the telegraphic service in the late Qing
locator: Modern Asian Studies 49(3), pp. 832–857; abstract, references and thesis-origin footnote; online 2013
scope_limit: Abstract-only mechanism argument. Cannot audit rates, actual machine purchases, investor instructions or customer composition.
evidence_lineage: Developed from 2008 Yale thesis on Grand Council communication systems; bibliography includes Sheng records and telegraph histories. Gao/Lei cites Yoon, so the two are not independent for institutional background.
inspection_detail: Publisher abstract and references inspected. Prices, reliability and dividends arguments attributed to Yoon, not treated as directly verified administrative statistics.

title: 盛宣怀与上海电报局改制 / Sheng Xuanhuai and the Systematic Reform of Shanghai Telegraph Bureau in the Late Qing Dynasty
locator: Studies in Qing History, 2019(3), pp. 110–125; Chinese/English abstracts and references
scope_limit: Abstract-only. Evidence concerns officials/investors, not public consent or successful democratization. PDF icon did not yield article text in browser extraction.
evidence_lineage: Bibliography identifies Sheng Xuanhuai archives, unpublished letters, industrial telegrams, Qing Veritable Records, Yuan Shikai works, and modern compilations. Documents not directly inspected here.
inspection_detail: Both language abstracts and bibliography read; author interpretation of conflicted official/investor interests explicitly attributed.

title: Décret concernant l’uniformité des poids et mesures, 12 février 1812
locator: Journal des mines, contemporary reproduction, printed pp. 453–454 (PDF pp. 1–2), articles 1–6
scope_limit: Prescriptive law proves authorized arrangements, not enforcement or approval. Scan includes unrelated decrees not used here.
evidence_lineage: Contemporary printed reproduction of imperial decree; direct legal text, later reproduced/discussed by S11–S13. Those accounts are not independent observations of compliance.
inspection_detail: Decree paragraphs read in extracted text; cached original scan. Article 1 retains base units; subsequent articles order adapted instruments, dual markings and continued official teaching.

title: Les origines du système métrique en France et la Convention du mètre de 1875, qui a ouvert la voie au Système international d’unités et à sa révision de 2018
locator: Comptes Rendus Physique 20, pp. 6–21; section 1 and especially pp. 13–14
scope_limit: Scholarly metrological history emphasizes institutions and scientific standards, with evaluative language about backward measures. Not a survey of popular practices. One toise equivalence in narrative appears erroneous; not used.
evidence_lineage: Draws on Academy/Bureau des longitudes records, Lenoir correspondence, legislation and earlier histories. 1837 law quoted, not independently inspected in original bulletin here.
inspection_detail: Full PDF fetched locally after web fetch 403; pp. 6–14 and selected captions read. Original Lyon newspaper law scan failed and is not counted as an inspected source.

title: Faites poids et mesures…
locator: Chroniques d’Archives 13 (September 2012), dossier, PDF pp. 2–10; introduction of metric system pp. 6–8
scope_limit: Local archival synthesis, not a systematic national adoption curve. Some narrative claims about habit and education are interpretations; long-run coda exceeds primary episode.
evidence_lineage: Cites local holdings L878, L293, L292, 159 M19, 2 O and PER series; incorporates earlier local scholarship. The individual registers/instruments have not been inspected here.
inspection_detail: Dossier read; law/practice, familiar task units, local correspondence tables, verification and continued rural language extracted. Rest of newsletter not relevant.

title: A History of the Metric System Controversy in the United States
locator: National Bureau of Standards Special Publication 345-10; introduction, pp. 7–11, especially pp. 10–11 and notes 51–53
scope_limit: Commissioned U.S. metric-study history; French prelude is secondary synthesis. Its judgments of popularity/confusion are not a French opinion survey.
evidence_lineage: French prelude inherits earlier metrological histories and legislation; overlaps S10/S11 for legal sequence. Materials and enforcement claims not independently checked against all cited originals.
inspection_detail: Full PDF cached; French prelude pp. 7–11 inspected, not entire U.S. controversy. Used narrowly for standards-distribution shortfall and translated 1837 provisions.

title: The Shock of the Old: Technology and Global History since 1900 — Introduction (inspected excerpt)
locator: Introduction, printed pp. ix–xv; PDF pp. 1–7
scope_limit: University-hosted excerpt inspected, not the entire book. Used for historiographical design, not for unverified quantitative examples.
evidence_lineage: Historiographical interpretation; historical examples rely on the author’s cited scholarship, not independently reconstructed here.

title: If Technology Has Arrived Everywhere, Why Has Income Diverged?
locator: July 20, 2017 manuscript, introduction pp. 1–3 and §4.1 p.18; selected sections inspected
scope_limit: Model-based analysis of selected technologies, not experimental identification of causes. The 25-technology sample is assumed representative; original dataset is unbalanced. Published version DOI 10.1257/mac.20150175.
evidence_lineage: CHAT technology adoption panel and Maddison income/population series; timing and intensity results share data and structural model assumptions.

title: Factors affecting the diffusion of technology
locator: Publisher chapter summary; chapter pp.189–210 not inspected
scope_limit: Summary supports only the distinction between invention and economic consequences through diffusion; detailed arguments not audited.
evidence_lineage: Author’s methodological argument, inspected only in publisher summary; not an independent empirical corroboration.
